Read Chainlink reference prices
Chainlink is the valuation reference for both underlying tokens. Each feed must be within the market's maximum feed age.
Compute token amounts from liquidity
The token amounts behind one vault token are computed from the pool's liquidity math at the reference price. For Uniswap v3 positions, they are computed from the position's liquidity and range.
Check against the pool TWAP
The approved AMM TWAP is compared with the Chainlink-derived price. It is only a consistency check. It is not averaged with the Chainlink price and does not replace it.
Report value with no haircut
LPOracle reports the full value of the liquidity per vault token. It does not discount for impermanent loss, slippage or liquidation costs.
Apply the Collateral Factor separately

Borrowing limits come from the reserve's Collateral Factor, where LPCollateralFactor = min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor. BorrowingCapacity = LPPositionValue × LPCollateralFactor. Collateral Risk sets the borrower's interest premium. It is not a haircut.
Uniswap v2 LP tokens
Chainlink + pool liquidity math + TWAP consistency check
Supported. 1 vault-token base unit per LP-token base unit.
Uniswap v3 positions (full-range or approved range)

Uniswap v4, Curve, Balancer, Aerodrome, SushiSwap and other AMMs
Not supported. Adding any of them requires a separate review and governance approval, including approval of its pricing method.
How LPOracle values vault tokens, and what the Aave Adapter allows when price checks fail.

Avana's LPOracle prices each vault token from the pool's liquidity math at Chainlink prices. Chainlink is the valuation reference, and the pool's TWAP is a second check. For concentrated positions, token amounts are computed from the position's liquidity and range at the reference price.
LPOracle reports the value of the liquidity per vault token with no haircut. How much of that value can support debt is set separately, through each reserve's Collateral Factor on the Borrow Spoke.

Valuation and borrowing limits are kept separate. The oracle reports what the position is worth. The Collateral Factor and pool risk factor account for range, price sensitivity, pool depth and expected liquidation costs.
Vault-token value depends on:
Each vault token is priced as the value of the two token amounts it represents:
VaultTokenPrice = q0·P0 + q1·P1
q0, q1
Amounts of token0 and token1 represented by one vault token. They are computed at the reference price from the pool's liquidity math and, for Uniswap v3, the position's range.
P0, P1
Chainlink reference prices for token0 and token1.
No haircut
The result is the full value of the liquidity. Risk adjustments are applied through the Collateral Factor, not in the price.
Vault tokens have 18 decimals and are minted 1:1 with liquidity. There is no scaling factor or exchange rate, so the oracle cannot affect how many vault tokens are issued.
LP valuation is not a single spot-price read. The path from prices to borrowing capacity has these steps:
LPOracle prices only selected Uniswap v2 LP tokens and Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum mainnet. Each approved pool has its own vault token, and so does each fee tier and range where applicable.
AMM / Position Type
Oracle Source
Notes

The approved AMM TWAP is a consistency check on the Chainlink-derived price. It is not an average of the two prices and does not replace Chainlink. It detects when pool state and reference prices disagree.
Uniswap v2
The pool's TWAP over the market's configured window is compared with the price implied by Chainlink. The window length is set per market.
Uniswap v3
The position's token amounts are computed from its liquidity and range. Before they are accepted, the pool's TWAP is compared with the Chainlink-derived price.
Tolerance
Each market has an allowed price deviation. If the TWAP is outside it, the Aave Adapter blocks new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals.
Chainlink stays the reference
When the TWAP is outside tolerance, repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price. The TWAP is never used as the valuation price.
Other AMMs
Avana defines TWAP sources only for Uniswap v2 and v3. A TWAP source for another AMM is defined in that AMM's review and approved by governance.
Allowed deviation and maximum feed age

Each market sets an allowed deviation between the TWAP and the Chainlink-derived price, and a maximum feed age. The four conditions below determine what remains available. Separately, the Guardian can freeze a market by freezing both the vault-token reserve and the GHO reserve on its Borrow Spoke.
Chainlink valid, TWAP within tolerance
Normal operation.
Chainlink valid, TWAP outside tolerance
The Aave Adapter blocks new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals. Repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price.
Chainlink stale or invalid, cached price within maximum age
The last valid price is used. New borrowing and voluntary withdrawals are blocked. Repayment and liquidation continue.
Cached price past maximum age
Liquidations pause until the feed recovers or governance approves a backup feed. Repayment continues.

Pledge: moves a Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position into the custody of the LP Vault. The Adapter mints vault tokens 1:1 through the Collateralization Module. It supplies them through the borrower's Position Proxy and enables them as collateral.
Borrow: borrows GHO from the Avana Hub through the Borrow Spoke. The TWAP and stale-price gates apply.
Repay: available at any time unless the Adapter is paused.
Withdraw: allowed only if the account stays healthy. The Adapter burns the matching vault tokens, and the LP Vault releases the LP tokens or NFT with uncollected fees.
The borrower entry point for deposits, borrowing, repayment and withdrawal, acting through each borrower's Position Proxy.

The Aave Adapter is the borrower's entry point to Avana. It coordinates deposits with the LP Vault and the Collateralization Module. When a position is pledged, the Adapter mints vault tokens and supplies them through the borrower's Position Proxy as collateral. Borrowing, repayment and withdrawal also go through the Adapter.

The Aave Adapter does not set risk parameters or collateral values. Collateral Factors, health checks and liquidation eligibility come from the Borrow Spoke, LPOracle and governance-approved parameters. Related pages:
Borrow Spoke
Liquidation Framework

A dedicated Position Proxy holds each borrower's Aave position. Every borrower action (deposit, borrow, repay, withdraw) therefore passes through the Aave Adapter and Avana's controls. Partial-settlement liquidations do not go through the Aave Adapter. In partial settlement, LPVaultSwap calls the Borrow Spoke directly. In full-position settlement, the Aave Adapter withdraws and burns all vault tokens for the position so the LP Vault can release it.

The Aave Adapter enforces the TWAP and stale-price gates. If the pool TWAP is outside tolerance, it blocks new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals. If the Chainlink feed is stale or invalid, it blocks new borrowing and voluntary withdrawals. Repayment continues in both cases.

A withdrawal is allowed only if the account stays healthy afterward. The Aave Adapter then burns the matching vault tokens. The LP Vault releases the LP tokens or NFT together with any uncollected fees.
The Aave Adapter is upgradeable, behind a timelock that Avana Labs cannot bypass. Contract addresses are published after deployment is approved.
Borrowers can call the contracts directly, without Avana's frontend. They keep the ability to repay and make permitted withdrawals.
Only positions that pass the Risk Module's pool and limit checks can be deposited. The Aave Adapter does not decide which pools are approved.

strings: Glossary
Definitions of Avana protocol terms, including the Avana Hub, Borrow Spokes, LP Vault, vault tokens, Collateral Factor, LPOracle and settlement modes.
Core Concepts
Protocol Components
Financial Terms
Risk & Security
Metrics
Disclaimers
A standard, unmodified Aave V4 Hub owned by the Aave DAO. It holds a capped GHO credit line allocated through the GHO Reserve. Only approved Avana Borrow Spokes can draw from it.
Avana Borrow Spoke

A standard Aave V4 Spoke owned by the Aave DAO. It holds collateral-only vault-token reserves for one market category. It lends GHO under each reserve's Collateral Factor, Collateral Risk and liquidation parameters.
Avana Lend Spoke
An Aave V4 Spoke that Aave governance approves separately. It adds direct lender supply to the Avana Hub and borrowing of assets other than GHO.
Hub-and-Spoke Architecture
The Aave V4 design in which liquidity sits in a Hub and collateral rules sit in Spokes. Avana uses standard Aave V4 Hub and Spoke contracts and keeps all Avana-specific logic in its own contracts.
An approved operator that calls LPVaultSwap to liquidate unhealthy accounts. At least two keeper operators run: Avana Labs and at least one independent operator.

A liquidity position in a supported AMM pool. Avana supports selected Uniswap v2 LP tokens and Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum mainnet. Uniswap v3 is limited to full-range positions and specifically approved ranges.
Depositing an LP position into the LP Vault. A Pledge changes custody but does not remove liquidity from the pool.
The Avana contract that holds pledged LP tokens and NFTs. It records each position's owner, market, backing and status. It releases a position only through an approved withdrawal or settlement.

A transfer-restricted, collateral-only ERC-20 record (18 decimals) that represents pledged liquidity 1:1 on an Avana Borrow Spoke. There is one vault token per approved pool, and per range where applicable. It has no owner, no secondary market and no emissions.
Position Proxy

A dedicated contract that holds each borrower's Aave position. Every deposit, borrow, repayment and withdrawal therefore passes through Avana's controls. In full-position markets it also carries settlement authority.
Collateral Factor
The share of a vault token's value that supports debt: LPCollateralFactor = min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor.
Pool Risk Factor
A per-market reduction applied once to the lower underlying Collateral Factor. It reflects range, price sensitivity, pool depth and expected liquidation costs.
Borrowing Capacity
LPPositionValue × LPCollateralFactor. Capacity also depends on existing debt, exposure caps, available GHO liquidity and oracle checks.
Market Category

One of three groups of approved markets, each with its own Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps: Stable LP (candidate USDC/USDT), Correlated LP (candidate wstETH/WETH) and Blue-chip/stable LP (candidate WETH/USDC).
Aave's stablecoin and the only asset borrowers can borrow from Avana.
GHO Credit Line
A capped GHO allocation from the Aave DAO to the Avana Hub through the GHO Reserve. Each increase is subject to conditions and governance approval.
Borrowing Rate
BaseRate × (1 + UserRiskPremium). For example, a 50% risk premium on a 4.5% base rate gives 6.75%.
The Avana Hub GHO base rate, which is at least the Core Hub GHO base rate.
User Risk Premium

The premium added to the base rate, set from the Collateral Risk of the borrower's collateral. With several collateral reserves, it is a weighted average. Aave V4 updates it on borrow, withdrawal, collateral change and on request.
Collateral Risk
A per-reserve setting on the Borrow Spoke that determines the borrower's interest premium. It is not a haircut on collateral value.
Health Factor
Collateral value after Collateral Factors, divided by outstanding GHO debt. An account becomes liquidatable when its health factor falls below 1.
Partial Settlement

The settlement mode for Uniswap v2 and selected Aerodrome or Uniswap v3 markets. LPVaultSwap calls Aave V4's standard liquidation with a GHO flash loan. Only the liquidity needed to restore health is removed, so the borrower keeps the rest of the position.
Full-Position Settlement

The settlement mode for most AMMs that use NFTs. LPVaultSwap repays the debt with a flash loan and settles the whole position through an approved route. Any surplus after debt, fees and costs returns to the borrower.
Liquidation Bonus
Aave V4's liquidation incentive in partial-settlement markets. It funds the keeper reward, execution costs and Avana's capped liquidation fee. It does not apply in full-position settlement.

Committed loss-coverage capital that LPVaultSwap draws on within a liquidation if proceeds fall short. If the reserve cannot cover the shortfall, the transaction reverts, and debt and collateral stay unchanged. It counts only once it is funded.
Avana's oracle for vault tokens. It prices each vault token from the pool's liquidity math at Chainlink prices (VaultTokenPrice = q0·P0 + q1·P1) and applies no haircut.

A consistency check against the pool's time-weighted average price. It is not averaged into the price. If the TWAP moves outside tolerance, new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals are blocked. Repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price.

The borrower's entry point to Avana. It coordinates deposits with the LP Vault and Collateralization Module, then mints and supplies vault tokens. Borrowing, repayment and withdrawal also go through the AaveAdapter. It enforces the TWAP and stale-price gates but does not set risk parameters or collateral values.

The only contract that performs liquidations. It takes flash loans and runs each market's settlement route. It draws from the FirstLossReserve when needed and pays keepers, Avana and borrowers. It is not a spoke and cannot draw from the Avana Hub. It is owned by an Aave DAO executor, and its operational controls are held by an Avana Labs and Aave DAO service-provider multisig.
Checks market eligibility, the pilot allowlist, position-size limits and exposure limits at the pool, underlying-token and depositor level.
Sets the vault-token amount for each position at 1:1 with its liquidity and reconciles backing. The oracle cannot affect issuance.
Immutable, versioned contracts that execute approved exits. They redeem LP tokens, remove liquidity and collect fees.
Holds market definitions, contract mappings, Avana-side limits, oracle settings, settlement routes and fee terms.
LP Collateral
The value of LP positions held in the LP Vault and represented by vault tokens on Avana Borrow Spokes.
Outstanding Debt
The amount of GHO currently borrowed against vault-token collateral.
Credit-Line Usage
The share of the Avana Hub's GHO credit line that borrowers have drawn.
Borrowing Headroom
The difference between a borrower's current debt and their borrowing capacity on a Borrow Spoke.
Backing Reconciliation
The comparison of vault-token supply with LP Vault liquidity for each market, reported by AaveAdapterLens.
Pool Approval

Only approved pools can be used as collateral. New collateral pools are published for a two-week review before listing approval. Meme-token pools and pools without enough liquidity history or reliable external pricing are excluded.
Pilot Allowlist

During the pilot, only allowlisted depositors can pledge positions. Each market has minimum and maximum position sizes, and each account has a limit on positions. Governance can remove the allowlist once pilot criteria are met.
Exposure Caps
Limits checked at the pool, underlying-token and depositor level, including a limit on the share of a pool's liquidity. Hub add and draw caps also limit flows per Borrow Spoke.
Emergency Guardian

A multisig that can pause, freeze and cancel. It cannot upgrade contracts, change parameters or move collateral. It can freeze a market by freezing both the vault-token reserve and the GHO reserve on the Borrow Spoke.
Governance Roles

The Aave DAO owns the Avana Hub and Borrow Spokes and holds pause and freeze roles over Avana's contracts. It can stop markets without Avana Labs. Avana Labs administers its own contracts within these permissions.
Upgrade Timelock
A delay on upgrades to Avana's upgradeable contracts, followed by a grace window. Avana Labs cannot bypass the delay. The Aave DAO can cancel queued upgrades.
Avana Umbrella
Avana's protocol safety module, named after Aave's Umbrella. It is third in the loss order, after dedicated first-loss capital and revenues committed to loss coverage.

strings: Key Concepts
Core concepts behind Avana: pledging LP positions, vault tokens, LPOracle valuation, Collateral Factors, GHO borrowing and settlement modes.
Core Insight
Borrowing Model
Oracle & Valuation
Borrowing Capacity
Health & Liquidation
Fee Treatment

Token collateral is usually a balance of a single asset, such as ETH, BTC or a stablecoin. An LP position is a changing combination of assets. Trades alter its inventory, prices change its value, and fees accrue over time. A concentrated-liquidity position also depends on its range and may become one-sided as prices move.

Avana therefore sets risk parameters per market. Each approved pool (and range, where applicable) has its own vault token. Each market has its own pool risk factor, settlement mode, TWAP window, allowed price deviation and maximum feed age. Each of the three market categories (Stable LP, Correlated LP and Blue-chip/stable LP) has its own Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps.

Users pledge an approved Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position to the LP Vault. A Pledge changes custody but does not remove liquidity, so the position keeps earning fees. A Uniswap v3 position stops earning fees while it is out of range.
The Collateralization Module mints vault tokens 1:1 with the pledged liquidity. The AaveAdapter supplies them to the market's Avana Borrow Spoke through the borrower's Position Proxy.
The borrower then borrows GHO from the Avana Hub. The Borrow Spoke applies vault-token risk parameters, and the Hub keeps GHO liquidity and debt accounting.

The LPOracle prices each vault token from the pool's liquidity math. It derives the token amounts behind each vault token and values them at Chainlink prices: VaultTokenPrice = q0·P0 + q1·P1. For Uniswap v3, the amounts come from the position's liquidity and range at the reference price.
The oracle applies no haircut. Each reserve's Collateral Factor handles risk separately, and Collateral Risk sets the borrower's interest premium.

Chainlink is the valuation reference. The pool's TWAP is a consistency check. It is not averaged into the price and does not replace Chainlink. If the TWAP moves outside tolerance, new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals are blocked. Repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price.

Borrowing capacity is the position's value multiplied by the reserve's Collateral Factor: LPCollateralFactor = min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor. The pool risk factor is applied once. It reflects range, price sensitivity, pool depth and expected liquidation costs.

Capacity also depends on existing debt, exposure caps, available GHO liquidity and oracle checks. The borrowing rate is BaseRate × (1 + UserRiskPremium). With several collateral reserves, the premium is a weighted average.
An illustrative example of how each reserve's factor is derived is in
Collateral Factors
Health factor compares collateral value, after each reserve's Collateral Factor, with outstanding GHO debt. An account becomes eligible for liquidation when its health factor falls below 1.

Only approved keepers can call LPVaultSwap. LPVaultSwap takes a GHO flash loan, repays the debt and settles the LP collateral in one transaction. Uniswap v2 and some Uniswap v3 markets use partial settlement, which removes only the liquidity needed to restore health. Markets where partial removal is not suitable use full-position settlement, which returns any surplus to the borrower.

Pledged positions stay in the pool and keep earning trading fees. A Uniswap v3 position earns fees only while it is in range. When a borrower withdraws, the LP Vault releases the LP tokens or NFT together with any uncollected fees. Withdrawal is allowed only if the account stays healthy.

Carol owes 20,000 USDC. Aave's bonus is 2%. The FLASH_BORROWER role is pending on Base, so the Base Pool charges 5 bps against Base's maxFlashFeeBps of 10.

The Base sequencer restarts at 10:00:00. At 10:20:00 Carol's health factor is 0.9997. A keeper call reverts with SequencerGrace, because 0.9997 is not below the grace threshold of 0.95. The USDC/USD feed last published 21 hours earlier (75,600 s, within 88,200 s), so the price is fresh. An account at a health factor of 0.93 is liquidated at 10:20.

At 11:00:02, the first 2 s Base block after the 3,600 s grace period, keeper K2 calls the Lens preview (a repayment of 2,000 USDC) and then liquidate with debtToCover 2,000 USDC, keeperFunds 0, flashAmount 2,000 USDC, PrimaryThenBackup, a deadline 120 s (60 Base blocks) ahead, minPayout 25 USDC and maxShortfall 0.
The flash source can lend well above 2,000 USDC. The premium is 1 USDC, and 1,000,000 × 10,000 = 10,000,000,000 is at most 10 × 2,000,000,000.

Aave repays D = 2,000 USDC and seizes c = 2,000 × 1.02 / 2.00 = 1,020 vault tokens. The Slipstream LP Vault checks the pool lock through Slipstream's own slot layout, then unwinds about 1,020 USDC and 1,020 USDT.

Floor: costsBps = 5 and s = min(100, ⌊10,000 × 195 / 10,200⌋) = 100. V = 2,040 USDC and φD = 1 USDC. The floor is 2,019.6 − 0.000002 − 1 = 2,018.599998 USDC. The USDT route returns 1,018.50 USDC, so R = 2,038.50 USDC.

The Pool pulls 2,001 USDC. Conservation: 4,038.5 in equals 2,000 + 2,001 + 7.8 + 29.7 out. If the fee recipient were blocklisted by USDC's issuer, the 7.8 USDC would go to the payout escrow and be claimed later with claim.

Market 1 is a USDC/USDT 0.01% Uniswap v3 market with an exact range on the Uniswap v3 Stable CDP Spoke of the Ethereum Stable LP Hub. The vault token has 6 decimals and is priced at $2.00. The debt reserve is USDC at $1.00 with a 1 USDC floor rounding allowance, a 100 bps slippage allowance and Avana's 20% share. Avana holds FLASH_BORROWER on the Ethereum Core Pool, so the premium is 0. Aave's bonus is 10,200 bps with a liquidation fee of 0.
The keeper flash-borrows 9,800 USDC with keeperFunds 0.
Aave repays D = 9,800 USDC and seizes 9,800 × 1.02 / 2.00 = 4,998 vault tokens.
The pool sits at tick 3 and the oracle at tick 2. No spot check applies; the unwound tokens are worth at least V at oracle prices.
Floor: s = 100 bps, V = 9,996 USDC, U = 2 base units, floor 9,895.039998 USDC.
The LP Vault returns about 4,998 USDC and 4,998 USDT. The USDC leg needs no swap. The USDT route returns 4,952 USDC, above its leg minimum of 4,946.030395 USDC. R = 9,950 USDC.
Case
Base case
Routes beat the oracle
Weaker routes

Routes beat the oracle: Kr is capped at the oracle gain after the fee, 156.8, and the remaining 14 USDC goes to the borrower's wallet. If the wallet is on USDC's blocklist, the 14 USDC goes to the payout escrow credited to the wallet.
Weaker routes: with minPayout set to 110 USDC, the call reverts with PayoutTooLow(95,800,000, 110,000,000). A is unchanged at 39.2.

The same account can be liquidated by any address through the permissionless path, with debtToCover 9,800 USDC, callerFunds 0, flashAmount 9,800 USDC, a deadline 120 s ahead and minPayout 110 USDC. With R = 9,950 USDC the caller receives 110.8 USDC and Avana's fee is 39.2 USDC.
Same market. The account's last 0.3978 vault token (397,800 units) is seized for D = 0.78 USDC.
V = 0.7956 USDC and the slippage term is ⌈795,600 × 0.99⌉ = 787,644 base units.
The floor is max(0, 787,644 − 2 − 1,000,000) = 0. Without the rounding allowance, the floor of 0.787644 USDC would revert every attempt and the deficit would never be recorded.
A route returns R = 0.77 USDC. The rounding gap is 0.78 − 0.77 = 0.01 USDC.
Caller settings
Flash-funded, maxShortfall 0.02 USDC
The caller pays 0.01 USDC through the top-up. R′ = 0.78 USDC, Y = 0 and keeperOut = (0 + 0.78 + 0.78) − (0.78 + 0.78) = 0.
Flash-funded, maxShortfall 0
Reverts with InsufficientProceeds: the gap, not the floor, is short. The keeper resubmits with keeperFunds of 0.01 USDC, which closes the gap.
Caller-funded 0.78 USDC, no flash loan
The gap is 0, Y = 0 and keeperOut = (0.78 + 0.77) − 0.78 = 0.77 USDC: a 0.01 USDC loss the caller accepts through minPayout.
In every case the caller pays the rounding gap. No protocol balance is drawn, and any deficit the call records is reported normally.

Same market 1. GHO is debt reserve 0, drawn by the CDP Spoke from the Stable LP Hub's GHO credit line at Aave's fixed $1 price, with a floor rounding allowance of 1 GHO. The vault-token reserve is reserve 1, with a Collateral Factor of 2,812 bps, a maximum bonus of 10,500, a bonus factor of 4,000, a health factor for the maximum bonus of 0.90 and a target health factor of 1.10. Alice's proxy P holds 141,232 vault tokens (282,464 USD) and owes 79,452.85 GHO.

A USDT move takes P's health factor to 282,464 × 0.2812 / 79,452.85 ≈ 0.9997. Keeper K1 calls the Lens preview for P and reserve 0: bonus 10,200, debt to target (1.10 × 79,452.85 − 79,428.88) / (1.10 − 1.02 × 0.2812) ≈ 9,800.2 GHO. The Ethereum Pool's idle GHO covers 9,800 GHO, so the preview sets flashAmount to 9,800 GHO and keeperFunds to 0.

K1 calls liquidate for P, market 1 and reserve 0 with debtToCover 9,800 GHO, keeperFunds 0, flashAmount 9,800 GHO, PrimaryThenBackup, a deadline 120 s ahead, minPayout 110 GHO and maxShortfall 0. LPVaultSwap checks the deadline, takes the lock, and checks the keeper, the proxy, the reserve and that 0 + 9,800 ≥ 9,800. It does not read the pause state.

LPVaultSwap reads the registry, pokes the LP Oracle (Live; USDC/USD and USDT/USD answers 20 hours and 3 hours old, within 88,200 s), finds the sequencer gate open on Ethereum, reads the health factor 0.9997, the bonus 10,200 and a liquidation fee of 0, and confirms the Hub's shares equal its assets.

LPVaultSwap calls the flash source for 9,800 GHO. The source checks the GHO reserve is active and flash-enabled, idle GHO covers 9,800 and the premium is 0 (role granted), then calls the Pool's flashLoan. The Pool sends 9,800 GHO to the source and calls it back; the source forwards 9,800 GHO to LPVaultSwap and calls onFlashLoan, which runs the next five steps.
Collateralization's beginSeizure snapshots P's 141,232,000,000 supplied shares.

LPVaultSwap approves the Spoke for 9,800 GHO and calls the liquidation for collateral reserve 1, debt reserve 0 and P, with receiveShares false. Aave restores D = 9,800 GHO to the Hub and the Hub transfers 4,998 vault tokens to LPVaultSwap. No deficit.

The AaveAdapter burns the 4,998 vault tokens. Collateralization checks that the share drop and the supply drop both equal c, debits P's largest record, and has the Uniswap v3 LP Vault unwind 4,998,000,000 units. The LP Vault collects only the principal, about 4,998 USDC and 4,998 USDT, to LPVaultSwap.

The floor in GHO is 9,895.0399980002 GHO (U = 0.0000019998 GHO). The USDC→GHO and USDT→GHO primary routes, through fixed DEX pools, return 4,976 and 4,974 GHO: R = 9,950 GHO and the rounding gap is 0.
onFlashLoan sends 9,800 GHO back to the flash source and returns; the source approves the Pool for 9,800 GHO, which pulls it.

Waterfall: Y = 150, A = 39.2, Kr = 110.8, B = 0 and keeperOut = 110.8 GHO, at least minPayout. LPVaultSwap sends 39.2 GHO to the fee recipient and 110.8 GHO to K1, emits LiquidationSettled and releases the lock.

After the transaction P holds 136,234 vault tokens (272,468 USD) against 69,652.85 GHO, a health factor of 272,468 × 0.2812 / 69,652.85 = 1.09999. Alice keeps the rest of her position and all of its fees. Had K1 called the Spoke's liquidation function directly, the Hub's vault-token transfer to K1 would have reverted with UnauthorizedRecipient.
What happens
Expired market

An account in Expired market 7 holding $20,000 of vault tokens and owing 6,400 GHO has a health factor near 0, because Expired collateral counts as almost 0. A call naming market 7 reverts with StalePrice until a fresh price or a standby price route arrives; the keeper then liquidates at the fresh price.
Stale debt price
USDC accepted at 0.9999 and Expired, with a 500 bps stress rise, counts at 1.049895 USD. The account can still be liquidated against its GHO debt; a call repaying USDC waits for a fresh USDC price.
Pool moved before the call

The pool is pushed to 2 USDT per USDC. The $10,000 position now holds tokens worth $10,606.60 at oracle prices. The liquidation unwinds at that price; each leg must still meet its oracle minimum, and the floor uses V = 10,000.
Third-party liquidation call

An attacker holding 1 USDC calls the Spoke's liquidation directly on an account at a health factor of 0.98. Aave sizes a seizure of 510,000 units, and the Hub's transfer reverts with UnauthorizedRecipient. The account is unchanged.
A 1,950 USDC whole-debt close sized at 2,047.5 USDC still settles after a 1-wei repayment: Aave pulls 1,949.999999 USDC and the caller payout is 1 wei lower.
Dust leg

USDC debt at $0.70 and a DAI leg of 0.000007349976535931 DAI at $0.05000016: the leg is worth less than one USDC base unit, so it is sent to the caller unswapped, R = 0, the floor is 0, and a caller-funded call repays the dust debt.
Small account on Base
An account owing 40 USDC with one record uses 1,550,000 gas. The keeper's part of the bonus is 0.54208 USDC, and Avana's keeper liquidates it whether or not that covers the gas.
Whole-debt close and record cap

An account owing 320 USDC whose preview returns a whole-debt close of 336 USDC is liquidated in one call with debtToCover 336 USDC. An account with 16 records uses 5,150,000 gas, still one transaction.
Worked Avana liquidations with full numbers, from Uniswap v3 on Ethereum and Slipstream on Base to fee variants, a dust gap and a GHO-debt walkthrough.

strings: Liquidation Flow
Step-by-step settlement of an Avana liquidation: checks, flash loan, Aave seizure, burn, unwind, swaps, recovery floor, flash repayment and payouts.
Overview
Notation
Settlement Steps
Flash Loan
Seizure, Burn and Unwind
Swap Legs
Recovery Floor
Shortfall and Rounding Gaps
Flash Repayment
Payout Waterfall
Refused Payouts
Events
End State
Every step of one liquidation, in execution order, with the checks, formulas and payouts LPVaultSwap applies.

One call liquidates one account, in its one collateral market, against one debt reserve, and settles it in the same transaction. Every amount is measured as a balance change within the call, never as an absolute balance and never from another contract's return value. If any step fails, the whole transaction reverts.

When the call uses a flash loan, the steps from holding the debt asset to the shortfall check run inside the flash-loan callback. Without a flash loan they run directly after the caller's funds are pulled. No step before the unwind touches the market's own pool.
Who can call, and when an account is eligible, is on the design page:
Liquidation Design

Every settlement amount is in base units of the repaid debt asset: 6 decimals for USDC and USDT, 18 for GHO and WETH. Prices are 8-decimal USD. Basis points use 10,000 = 100%. ⌊·⌋ rounds down and ⌈·⌉ rounds up.
Symbol
Meaning
debtToCover, the most debt asset Aave may pull
Caller funds pulled at entry (keeperFunds or callerFunds)
Debt asset flash-borrowed (flashAmount)
φ, φD
Flash premium on F; premium on the part of F that covered the debt, min(F, D). Both are 0 when F is 0 or the premium is waived.
Debt asset Aave pulled in its liquidation call
Vault-token units LPVaultSwap received
b, lf, bNet
Aave liquidation bonus, Aave liquidation fee (0 by the listing settings), net bonus, in bps where 10,000 means no bonus
Pc, Pdebt
Vault-token and debt-asset prices served to Aave
Oracle value of the seized units in the debt asset
One raw unit of each unwound token, valued in the debt asset
minOut
Recovery floor
R, R′
Debt asset recovered from the seized collateral; R plus the caller's shortfall top-up
Rounding gap, max(0, D + φD − K − R), paid by the caller
Y, G
Realized surplus max(0, R′ − D − φD); oracle gain max(0, V − D − φD)
A, Kr, B
Avana fee, keeper reward, borrower surplus; A + Kr + B = Y
keeperOut
The caller's payout, keeper or permissionless caller
The steps below run in this exact order.
Step
What happens
Deadline
LPVaultSwap reverts with DeadlineExpired if the block timestamp is past the deadline, before the lock and before any external call.
Lock and entry checks

LPVaultSwap takes the chain's protocol lock (LockHeld if held), then checks the amounts (InvalidAmount), a frozen caller (AddressIsFrozen), the approved keeper on the keeper path (NotApprovedKeeper), the proxy (UnknownProxy), the debt reserve (UnknownDebtReserve) and the route mode. The pause state is not read.
Resolve the market

From the MarketRegistry: the CDP Spoke, home Hub, collateral reserve, vault token, AMM integration and its LP Vault, pool and exact range, the market's tokens and swap routes; the debt reserve's asset, decimals, funding Hub, price source and Avana Umbrella (UnknownMarket on mismatch).
Poke oracles and check prices

LPVaultSwap pokes the market's LP Oracle and the repaid reserve's DebtOracle, then checks the health factor (NotLiquidatable), the collateral price (StalePrice), recovery grace (GraceHealthFactor), Hub shares against assets (SharesNotEqualAssets) and the debt price (DebtPriceStale).
Sequencer gate
Down reverts with SequencerDown. During the grace period after a restart, only accounts below a health factor of 0.95 pass (SequencerGrace). Ethereum is always open.
Read the bonus
The health factor, the bonus b and the liquidation fee lf from the Spoke, read in the same call and block as the liquidation, so they equal what Aave applies; the debt price Pdebt.
LPVaultSwap reads no pool spot price. A moved pool never reverts the call or changes its route mode.
Fund
Pulls K from the caller if K is above 0 (FundingMismatch unless exactly K arrives). If F is above 0, borrows F through the flash source; the following steps run inside the callback.
Hold the debt asset
LPVaultSwap requires its debt-asset balance to have risen by at least X (FundingMismatch). The debt asset is never bought with another asset.
beginSeizure
Collateralization checks the lock and the caller, checks Hub shares against assets, and stores the proxy's supplied shares and the vault token's total supply in transient storage.
liquidationCall

LPVaultSwap approves the Spoke for exactly X and calls the liquidation with receiveShares set to false, then resets the approval. Aave validates, sizes the repayment, pulls D to the funding Hub and sends c vault tokens from the home Hub to LPVaultSwap. It reports deficits if the call empties the collateral.
Measure D and c
Both measured as balance changes. If c is 0 the call reverts with NothingSeized. The unused X − D stays in LPVaultSwap to repay flash principal or return to the caller; it is never swapped.
Open the recovery window
LPVaultSwap records its balance of each market token and of the debt asset. Caller funds, flash principal and the unused debt asset stay outside the window of R.
burnSeized
The AaveAdapter, the vault token's only burner, burns the c units from LPVaultSwap's balance (SeizedUnitsBurned).
settleSeizure

Collateralization checks the snapshot, the pool lock, that the share drop equals c and that the supply drop equals c. It reconciles any earlier unsettled seizure of the proxy, debits c units from the proxy's records, and has the LP Vault unwind exactly those units.
Measure the unwind
LPVaultSwap measures the amount aᵢ of each market token it received. Uncollected fees never enter these amounts.
LPVaultSwap computes the net bonus, the effective slippage, V, U and the floor minOut in the debt asset, and each leg's minimum.
Swap legs

Each token that is not the debt asset is swapped over its route at its own oracle-derived minimum, in the route mode the caller set. R is the debt asset received from the start of the window to the end of conversion.
Shortfall check

The shortfall is max(0, minOut − R, D + φD − K − R). A floor gap above maxShortfall reverts with RecoveryBelowFloor; a rounding gap above it reverts with InsufficientProceeds. Otherwise the shortfall is pulled from the caller.
Waterfall
LPVaultSwap computes Y, A, Kr, B and keeperOut (InsufficientProceeds if negative), then checks keeperOut against minPayout (PayoutTooLow).
Repay the flash loan
LPVaultSwap sends F + φ to the flash source, which approves the Pool for exactly that amount; the Pool pulls it.
Pay out
A to the fee recipient, then B to the borrower's wallet, then keeperOut to the caller, all in the debt asset. Zero amounts are skipped. A refused transfer goes to the payout escrow.
Event and lock
LPVaultSwap emits LiquidationSettled and releases the lock. Its net balance change is 0 in every token, and every allowance it granted is 0.

Each chain has one flash source contract, read from the MarketRegistry's flashSource and replaceable by the chain's timelock at the normal delay. Its only implementation calls the chain's Aave V3 Pool flashLoan with one asset and no debt mode: the Core Pool on Ethereum, and the Base Pool at 0xA238Dd80C259a72e81d7e4664a9801593F98d1c5. Aave V4 has no flash loans. The simple flash-loan function does not waive the premium for the FLASH_BORROWER role, so the full flashLoan call is used.
Checks before lending
The lender must not be the CDP Spoke's home Hub or the reserve's funding Hub (FlashSourceIsHub). A liquidation must not repay a Hub with that Hub's own liquidity, which would hide a liquidity crunch.
The flash source's available liquidity must be at least F (FlashLiquidityShort).
The Pool reserve of the asset must be active, not paused and enabled for flash loans, with idle liquidity of at least F (FlashSourcePaused, InsufficientFlashLiquidity).
The premium must pass the cap below (FlashFeeTooHigh).
φ × 10,000 ≤ maxFlashFeeBps × F

The comparison is exact, in base units on both sides. maxFlashFeeBps is 10 on Ethereum and Base, above the Aave V3 premium of 5 bps. The premium is waived when the Pool grants the flash source the FLASH_BORROWER role; governance then lowers maxFlashFeeBps to 0 with tightenMaxFlashFeeBps at the short delay. The premium is a settlement cost, paid before Avana's fee.

Example: a flash loan of 2,000 USDC at 5 bps has a premium of 1 USDC. 1,000,000 × 10,000 = 10,000,000,000 is at most 10 × 2,000,000,000 = 20,000,000,000, so the loan proceeds. At 11 bps (2.2 USDC) the check fails and the call reverts; the caller resubmits fully caller-funded.
Callbacks

The Pool calls the flash source's executeOperation, which accepts only the Pool as caller, itself as initiator, one asset, and the asset and amount it requested (InvalidFlashCallback). It forwards the amount it received to LPVaultSwap and calls LPVaultSwap's onFlashLoan. LPVaultSwap accepts that callback only from the chain's flash source, with an active settlement context, the reserve's debt asset, an amount equal to its own balance change, and the lock held. The context carries only an identifier; the validated parameters stay in transient storage.
Aave liquidation

The standard Spoke validates the call (not a self-liquidation, amount above 0, reserves not paused, collateral supplied, debt drawn in the reserve, health factor below 1), sizes the repayment against its target health factor with its dynamic bonus and dust rule, pulls D, and removes c vault tokens from the home Hub to LPVaultSwap. Receiving shares instead of tokens is disabled on the reserve, so LPVaultSwap always passes false.
Burn and ledger checks

The AaveAdapter burns the c units, then Collateralization checks that the drop in the proxy's supplied shares equals c (DebitMismatch) and that the drop in the vault token's supply equals c (SupplyDropMismatch). Collateralization reads the Spoke, Hub, reserve and vault token only from the vault token's immutables, never from the caller. It also refuses to unwind while the pool is inside a callback (PoolLocked), reading each AMM's own slot layout for that check only.
Record walk

Collateralization debits c units from the proxy's records, largest credited record first, ties by lowest record ID. It stops at the first record that covers the remainder, so at most one record is partly debited. A record at 0 units stays open for its depositor. An account holds at most 16 records per market. Every record of a market has the market's exact range, so the units are interchangeable and the order has no economic effect. If the records hold fewer than c units, the call reverts with InsufficientCredit.

Before debiting c, Collateralization reconciles any shares an earlier, unsettled seizure took without a debit. It debits those units too, unwinds them into its pending balance, and emits SeizureReconciled. Those tokens are settled later by settlePending and never paid out inside the liquidation.
Unwind

For each debited record, the market's LP Vault removes exactly the debited units and sends the principal to LPVaultSwap. For Uniswap v3 and Aerodrome Slipstream it calls decreaseLiquidity with zero minimums, then collect capped at the principal, so fees owed to the position stay with it for the depositor. Collateralization releases the record's exposure on a fixed basis: the remaining charge is the original charge times remaining units over original units, rounded up.
Example: a record pledged with 600,000,000 units and a 1,200 USD charge is debited 200,000,000 units. It keeps ⌈1,200 × 400 / 600⌉ = 800 USD of charge and releases 400 USD of cap.

For each market token and each enabled debt asset, the MarketRegistry records a primary and a backup swap route. Each route contract has a fixed path set at deployment, takes only LPVaultSwap as caller, and enforces the minimum output it receives (MinOutNotMet).

Route types: DexPath (fixed pool hops on Uniswap v3, Slipstream, Curve or Balancer), PegModule (a GHO Stability Module on Ethereum, backup slot of a GHO debt reserve only, or the Sky LitePSM for DAI or USDS into USDC), and WrapperThenDex (one unwrap step, then pool hops).
A route never trades through the market's own pool, which is being unwound in the same transaction. Any pool callback is accepted only from the pool fixed in the route.
The backup shares no external contract and no intermediate token, other than the debt asset, with the primary, so one failure cannot disable both.
A GHO Stability Module is never a primary route.
Listing requires both routes of every token to swap the full one-sided value of the largest position within the market's slippage allowance.
Per-leg minimum
Every leg runs with a minimum output derived from oracle prices, primary and backup alike. No swap of a liquidation runs without one.
minOutᵢ = max(1, ⌈Vlegᵢ × (10,000 − sLeg) / 10,000⌉ − Ulegᵢ − ⌊floorRoundingAllowance / k⌋)

Vlegᵢ is the leg's value in the debt asset at the LP Oracle's capped leg price, Ulegᵢ is one raw unit of the token in the debt asset, k is the number of legs swapped, and sLeg is the leg slippage (the effective slippage s, widened by a shortfall allowance as described below).

Example: a 4,998 USDT leg at 0.9998 USD into USDC, with sLeg of 100 bps, one leg swapped and a 1 USDC allowance: Vleg = 4,997.0004 USDC, and the minimum is 4,947.030396 − 0.000001 − 1 = 4,946.030395 USDC.
Dust legs, residues and failed routes

A token worth at most about one raw unit of the debt asset is a dust leg. It is not swapped: LPVaultSwap sends it whole to the caller and counts it as 0 toward R. Otherwise every route could return 0 for it and the account could never be liquidated.
Input or intermediate tokens a route returns unconverted count as 0 toward R and go to the caller (ResidueReturned).
A primary that reverts emits RouteFailed, its approval is reset to 0, and the backup is called. If no usable route converts a token, the call reverts with NoRouteAvailable.

Route records change only by timelock: setRoute at the normal delay (5 days), disableRoute and restoreRoute of a previously approved route at the short delay (12 hours). An operation that only restores routes can be cancelled only by the Aave governance executor.
Unwind at any pool price

The unwind runs at zero per-token minimums because the LP Oracle values a position at its fair composition, the minimum of its oracle value over all pool prices. Removing the liquidity at any pool price returns tokens worth at least V at oracle prices. What a moved pool can still distort is a swap, and every swap leg has its own oracle minimum. A spot gate would add nothing and would let anyone keep an underwater account alive by moving a thin pool before each attempt.

Example: a full-range USDC/USDT position worth $10,000 at $1.00 each holds about 5,000 of each token. An attacker moves the pool to 2 USDT per USDC. The position now holds 3,535.53 USDC and 7,071.07 USDT, worth $10,606.60 at oracle prices. A keeper seizes and unwinds it at that pool price, the USDT leg must still return its oracle minimum, and the floor is computed from V = 10,000.
The floor is computed in the debt asset, so the same rule serves GHO, USDC, WETH or any other debt reserve. It allows exactly the swap loss that Aave's net bonus can pay for after the flash premium.
costsBps = ⌈φ × 10,000 / F⌉ (0 when F = 0)
s = min(slippageAllowanceBps, ⌊10,000 × (bNet − 10,000 − costsBps) / bNet⌋), or 0 if not positive
V = ⌊c × Pc × 10^dd / (10^dv × Pdebt)⌋
U = Σᵢ ⌈pᵢ × 10^dd / (10^dᵢ × Pdebt)⌉ (a token that is the debt asset counts 1)
minOut = max(0, ⌈V × (10,000 − s) / 10,000⌉ − U − floorRoundingAllowance)
s solves (1 + bNet)(1 − s) ≥ 1 + costs, so the slippage term alone repays the debt and the flash premium. slippageAllowanceBps is 100 at launch.
V uses the prices Aave used for the seizure, so the floor measures swap loss only, never a price difference between Avana and Aave.

U and floorRoundingAllowance let dust liquidations settle. AMM removals and swaps round down by up to one raw unit per token. Without these terms a dust liquidation would revert on every attempt, and its deficit would never be recorded.
floorRoundingAllowance is set per debt reserve when it is enabled: one whole token for a USD stablecoin (1,000,000 for USDC, 10^18 for GHO) and 0.0005 WETH for WETH debt.
The floor depends on no caller input. V rounds down and the slippage term rounds up, both against the caller.

Example (Ethereum, USDC debt): c = 4,998 vault tokens at Pc = 2.00, bNet = 10,200 and no premium. s = min(100, ⌊10,000 × 200 / 10,200⌋) = 100. V = 9,996 USDC. With USDC at 1.0000 and USDT at 0.9998, U = 2 base units. minOut = 9,896.04 − 0.000002 − 1 = 9,895.039998 USDC.
After the swaps, LPVaultSwap computes the amount the caller must add:
shortfall = max(0, minOut − R, D + φD − K − R)
The first term is recovery below the floor. If it exceeds maxShortfall, the call reverts with RecoveryBelowFloor.
The second term is the rounding gap g: what the caller's own funds left uncovered of the debt and its flash premium. If it exceeds maxShortfall, the call reverts with InsufficientProceeds.
Otherwise LPVaultSwap pulls exactly the shortfall from the caller, and R′ = R + shortfall.

Rounding gaps are paid by the caller, never by a protocol balance, on the keeper and permissionless paths alike. The caller chose the liquidation's size and funding, so it pays the few base units of rounding that result.
A caller that allows a top-up also lets each leg run at a wider slippage, which keeps liquidations running at full size when routes trade below the oracle in a crash:
sLeg = min(9,999, s + min(maxShortfallBps, ⌊maxShortfall × 10,000 / V⌋))
maxShortfallBps is 1,000. Avana's fee does not fall when a shortfall is paid, and the borrower surplus is 0 in that case, so a caller's top-up never reaches the borrower.

Example: V = 12,422.6 USDC, s = 100 bps and maxShortfall = 200 USDC. The legs run at 260 bps, the routes return 12,174 USDC, 123.373998 USDC is pulled from the caller, and the liquidation settles at full size.

Before the callback returns, LPVaultSwap transfers enough of the debt asset to the flash source that its balance rises by F + φ, checked as a balance change. Unspent flash principal and the debt asset Aave did not pull repay the loan in the same transaction. The flash source approves the Pool for exactly F + φ, the Pool pulls it, and the flash source resets the allowance and checks that its own balance is unchanged (FlashRepayShort otherwise).

The premium on flash principal the debt did not need, φ − φD, is paid from the caller's payout only. If the surplus cannot pay it, the call reverts with InsufficientProceeds. A debt asset with a transfer fee is grossed up, and that cost also falls on the caller's payout.
Y = max(0, R′ − D − φD)
G = max(0, V − D − φD)
A = min(⌊G × avanaFeeShareBps / 10,000⌋, Y)
Kr = min(Y − A, G − A)
B = Y − A − Kr
keeperOut = (K + F + R′) − (D + F + φ + A + B)

Avana's fee A is 20% (avanaFeeShareBps = 2,000) of the oracle gain G, never above the realized surplus Y. While Y covers it, A depends only on the oracle value of the seizure and the debt repaid, never on how the caller swapped. Since A never exceeds Y, the fee alone never makes a liquidation revert.
The keeper reward Kr is the rest of the oracle gain, capped by what was realized.

The borrower surplus B is the recovery above the seized collateral's oracle value. It is non-zero only when the routes beat the oracle price, so a favourable price move during settlement goes to the borrower.
A + Kr + B = Y exactly. A rounds down, so rounding dust stays with the borrower.

keeperOut equals Kr plus the caller's unspent funds, minus the premium on unused flash principal and minus any shortfall the caller added. If it would be negative, the call reverts with InsufficientProceeds.
The debt asset is conserved: K + F + R + shortfall = D + (F + φ) + A + B + keeperOut. LPVaultSwap never keeps or creates the debt asset.
Payout order
The flash principal and premium F + φ, returned to the flash source inside the callback.
Avana's fee A to the fee recipient read from the ParameterStore. A zero fee recipient reverts with InvalidFeeRecipient.
The borrower surplus B to the borrower's wallet, the wallet the AaveAdapter records for the proxy (BorrowerSurplusPaid).
keeperOut to the caller.
No recipient is taken from calldata, nothing accumulates in LPVaultSwap, and every zero-amount transfer is skipped. Each payout is measured as the recipient's balance change.

Example (Ethereum, USDC debt): D = 9,800, V = 9,996, no premium, and the routes return R = 9,950 USDC. Y = 150, A = min(⌊196 × 0.2⌋, 150) = 39.2, Kr = min(110.8, 156.8) = 110.8, B = 0 and keeperOut = 110.8 USDC. With R = 10,010 USDC instead: Y = 210, A = 39.2, Kr = 156.8 and B = 14 USDC to the borrower.
Every payout (Avana's fee, the borrower surplus, the caller payout, a residue or a dust leg) uses a gas-limited delivery that cannot revert the liquidation:
LPVaultSwap requires enough gas left: ⌈100,000 × 64 / 63⌉ + 10,000 = 111,588 gas, else InsufficientGas. This stops a caller from starving the call to push a payout into the escrow.
It calls the token's transfer with exactly 100,000 gas and reads at most 32 bytes of return data.

If the transfer reverts, returns false or runs out of gas, LPVaultSwap approves the payout escrow for exactly the amount and calls its deposit, credited to the recipient. The liquidation continues. Only a revert of the deposit itself reverts the call.
The payout escrow keeps the contract name InKindEscrow. It is immutable, one per chain, with no owner, role or setter, and holding refused payouts is its only job. The credited account later calls
claim(token, recipient)
to receive its whole credit at an address it chooses. Deposits emit RemainderEscrowed and claims emit RemainderClaimed.

Example: a borrower's wallet is on USDC's blocklist and the liquidation owes it a 14 USDC surplus. The transfer fails, the 14 USDC is deposited in the escrow credited to the wallet, and the liquidation completes.

strings: Liquidators
How approved keepers and permissionless callers liquidate Avana accounts through LPVaultSwap: parameters, route modes, sizing, gas and failures.
Overview
Approved Keeper Path
Route Modes
Permissionless Path
Pending Settlement
Sizing a Call
Keeper Operations
Gas Model
Example: Permissionless Call
Failures and Responses
How approved keepers and any other address call LPVaultSwap, how to size a call, and what each failure means.

An account can be liquidated when its health factor is below 1 and the prices of its market and the repaid debt reserve are fresh. Every liquidation goes through LPVaultSwap, which has two liquidation entry points and one settlement entry point:
liquidate
: for approved keepers, with both route modes.
liquidatePermissionless
: for any address, with the PrimaryThenBackup route mode only.
settlePending
: for any address; settles stranded units and pays the caller nothing.

The caller is always msg.sender at LPVaultSwap, and every caller payout goes to msg.sender. No recipient, route, flash source, recovery-floor override or executable calldata is taken from the caller. Every amount is in base units of the debt asset being repaid.
Eligibility rules and the reasons liquidation is never paused are on the design page:
Liquidation Design
Approved keepers call
liquidate(LiquidationParams params)

, which returns a LiquidationResult. A caller that is not on LPVaultSwap's keeper list reverts with NotApprovedKeeper before any external call, and can use the permissionless path instead. Every approved keeper is operated by Avana.
Field
Meaning
Rule
proxy
The borrower's PositionProxy, the Aave account for one market
Must be a valid proxy of the market's vault token, else UnknownProxy
marketId
The collateral market to seize from
Must be the proxy's market; Registered, Active and Offboarding markets are accepted
debtReserveId
The debt reserve to repay
Must be enabled for the Spoke, else UnknownDebtReserve
debtToCover
The most debt asset Aave may pull, passed unchanged to Aave
Greater than 0; a bound, never an exact amount
keeperFunds
Debt asset pulled from the keeper at entry
keeperFunds plus flashAmount must be at least debtToCover, else InvalidAmount
flashAmount
Debt asset to flash-borrow through the chain's flash source
At most the source's idle liquidity, else FlashLiquidityShort
routeMode
PrimaryThenBackup or BackupOnly
Applied as set; no pool price changes it
minAmounts
Optional least amount of each market token the unwind must return
Empty, or one value per market token; it can only make the call revert
deadline
Last valid block timestamp, in seconds
Checked first, before the lock and any external call, else DeadlineExpired
minPayout
The smallest caller payout the caller accepts
Checked after the payout waterfall, else PayoutTooLow
maxShortfall
The most of the caller's own debt asset the call may pull after the swaps
Covers recovery below the floor and any rounding gap; 0 disables it

Each amount is at most 2^128 − 1. The deadline, minPayout and minAmounts change no amount, route or recipient: they can only make the call revert. The recovery floor is computed from oracle prices alone, so minPayout protects the caller while the floor protects Avana and the borrower.

The LiquidationResult returns the debt asset, the debt repaid, the units seized, the amount of each token the unwind returned, the amount recovered, the recovery floor, the flash premium, Avana's fee, the caller payout, the borrower surplus and the shortfall pulled from the caller.
Each market has, for each of its tokens and each enabled debt asset, a primary and a backup swap route recorded in the MarketRegistry. Both are held to the same recovery floor and per-leg minimums.
Mode
Behaviour
Available to
PrimaryThenBackup
Calls the primary route if it is usable. If the primary is not usable or reverts, emits RouteFailed for a revert and calls the backup if it is usable.
Approved keepers and permissionless callers
BackupOnly
Calls only the backup route of each token.
Approved keepers only

If no usable route converts a token, the call reverts with NoRouteAvailable. There is no in-kind fallback: the keeper waits for a restored or replaced route. A token that is itself the debt asset needs no route.
Any address can call
liquidatePermissionless(PermissionlessLiquidationParams params)
with no role, registration or agreement. It runs the same settlement as the keeper path, with these differences:
There is no keeper check.
The parameters have no route mode field: the call always runs PrimaryThenBackup, so a token with no working primary or backup route reverts with NoRouteAvailable.
The caller's own funds are passed as callerFunds instead of keeperFunds.

Everything else applies unchanged: the recovery floor and the optional shortfall top-up, the per-leg minimums, the price, sequencer and grace gates, the Hub share check, the deadline and the minimum payout. The caller pays its own rounding gap exactly as a keeper does, and receives the caller payout from the same waterfall.
Frozen callers

A caller on the chain's freeze list reverts with AddressIsFrozen on either liquidation function. The check runs right after the deadline check. A frozen wallet's own accounts are still liquidated like any other.
Approvals

Before calling, a caller approves LPVaultSwap for the debt asset it may have to provide: callerFunds, pulled at entry, plus maxShortfall, pulled after the swaps only if needed. A purely flash-funded call with maxShortfall set to 0 needs no approval. LPVaultSwap pulls exact amounts and measures each receipt as a balance change.
The function
settlePending(marketId, debtReserveId)

settles vault tokens that an earlier, unsettled seizure left at LPVaultSwap's fixed address. Collateralization keeps those units backed by real pool tokens in a pending balance, reconciled from the borrower's records during the next seizure or withdrawal. Any address can call it, the pause state is not read, and it never runs inside a liquidation.

Before taking the lock, LPVaultSwap requires a known market and a non-zero fee recipient. It settles the smaller of its own vault-token balance and Collateralization's pending units, and reverts with NothingPending if that is 0.
It reads the sequencer gate (SequencerDown while down), pokes the market's LP Oracle and applies the collateral price gate (StalePrice).
The AaveAdapter burns the units, and Collateralization releases the matching pool tokens to LPVaultSwap.
Each token is swapped into the settlement asset over the market's routes in PrimaryThenBackup mode, with a slippage allowance of the smaller of the market's allowance and 30 bps.
The recovery must reach the pending-settlement floor, else RecoveryBelowFloor.
The recovered amount is added to the Avana Umbrella (Coverage Spoke) of the settlement reserve's funding Hub and asset through its public fund function.
Any unconverted route residue goes to the fee recipient, or to the payout escrow if that transfer fails. The call emits PendingSettlementForwarded.

The caller receives nothing. The unsettled seizure already repaid debt and the borrower's records were already debited, so no waterfall applies. The Avana Umbrella is the layer that absorbs the loss of that incident. Each market names its settlement debt reserve at listing, its first enabled debt reserve, changeable at the normal delay.

A pending balance never blocks a liquidation. If the call reverts (price or sequencer gate, no usable route, the floor, or the Coverage Spoke refusing the funds), the tokens stay in custody backing the outstanding units, and anyone can repeat the call later.
Callers size each call from the Lens preview,
previewLiquidation(proxy, debtReserveId, deadline)
, which returns parameters that can be sent unchanged.
Set debtToCover to the previewed Aave amount: the repayment to Aave's target health factor, or the whole debt in the reserve when Aave's dust rule applies. There is no minimum size per call.
For a whole-debt close, the Lens quotes debtToCover with a 500 bps margin, rounded up, or stays at least 500 bps below Aave's dust boundary.
Set flashAmount to what the flash source can lend (its idle liquidity) and provide the rest as keeperFunds or callerFunds.
Set minPayout at least 1% below the previewed payout.
Set a deadline a short time ahead. 120 s is 10 Ethereum blocks and 60 Base blocks.
Set maxShortfall to cover the rounding gap the preview reports, and more if you are willing to top up a recovery below the floor.

Caller inputs are bounds, not exact values. A borrower who repays 1 wei, or repays enough to leave the debt just under the dust threshold, changes the amounts but not the outcome. Debt asset that Aave does not pull is not swapped: it repays flash principal or returns to the caller. Oversizing costs the caller only the flash premium on the unused part.

Example: the Lens previews a whole debt of 1,950 USDC with a 500 bps margin, so debtToCover is 2,047.5 USDC. A 1-wei repayment lands first. Aave pulls 1,949.999999 USDC, the 97.500001 USDC left over repays part of the flash loan, and the caller payout is 1 wei lower.

Size by simulation: re-run the Lens preview for each account at each new block and keep signed calls current, with flashAmount checked against the flash source's available liquidity and caller funds ready for the rest.
Submit through private order flow on Ethereum, so a pending call is not front-run or left in the public mempool.

Poke oracles: the LP Oracle and DebtOracle poke function is a permissionless cache write that keepers run on every feed update. LPVaultSwap also pokes the seized market and the repaid reserve inside every call. A poke needs a minimum amount of gas, and a gas-starved poke reverts the whole liquidation.
Send one account per transaction. Separate transactions never contend for the lock, which is released at the end of each call.
On Base, size each block's flash loans to the Base Pool's idle debt asset and spread larger liquidations over successive 2 s blocks.
Answer RecoveryBelowFloor with a shortfall top-up from keeper funds or with an arbitrage bundle, never with repeated halving, whose gas would exceed the debt each call repays.
When the flash source is short, paused or charges above the cap, resubmit with the whole amount as caller funds and flashAmount set to 0.
During an Aave halt of a CDP Spoke, stop sending calls for that market, keep the prepared calls current, and submit them in ascending health-factor order in the first block after the halt is lifted.
Liquidate an account with several debt reserves with successive calls until its health factor is at least 1 or a deficit is recorded. Skip accounts with no collateral left.

Failed floors and route failures are not counted on-chain. Avana's monitoring records each RouteFailed event and each RecoveryBelowFloor or NoRouteAvailable revert, and raises an alert at 3 failures in 1 hour on a market. The guardian freezes new borrowing on the market only once the approved routes are confirmed unable to settle valid liquidations at the required size; liquidation, repayment and debt-free exits stay open.
A flash-funded liquidation that touches n records uses about this much gas, measured on a fork of each chain:
One record: 1,550,000 gas.

An account holds at most 16 records per market, so the largest liquidation uses 5,150,000 gas. That is under half of the 16,777,216 per-transaction gas limit, so the largest account always fits in one transaction.
Ethereum counts execution gas. Base counts execution gas plus the L1 data fee of each transaction.
Avana budgets keeper gas per chain as the expected number of liquidations times the gas per liquidation times the gas price, plus the L1 data fee on Base. No protocol rule reads the gas price.

Example (Base): an account owing 40 USDC with one record falls below a health factor of 1. Its liquidation uses 1,550,000 gas. With a 2% bonus, a 0.3% swap cost and Avana's 20% share, the keeper's part of the bonus is 0.8 × (0.02 − 0.003 × 1.02) × 40 = 0.54208 USDC. Avana's keeper liquidates the account whether or not that covers the gas.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. This is Bob's USDC-debt account on a Uniswap v3 USDC/USDT market on Ethereum (worked through fully on the examples page), with no approved keeper acting.
Any address E calls the Lens preview for Bob's proxy and debt reserve 2 with a deadline 120 s ahead. It returns a repayment of 1,950 USDC and the PrimaryThenBackup mode.

E approves LPVaultSwap to pull up to 5 USDC, its maxShortfall, and calls liquidatePermissionless with debtToCover 1,950 USDC, callerFunds 0, flashAmount 1,950 USDC, empty minAmounts, minPayout 69 USDC and maxShortfall 5 USDC. If E were frozen, the call would revert with AddressIsFrozen.

The settlement runs as on the keeper path: a 1,950 USDC flash loan with a 0.975 USDC premium, 975 vault tokens seized and unwound, and the USDT leg swapped into USDC. The recovery is 2,040.30 USDC against a floor of 2,026.024998 USDC.
The shortfall is max(0, floor − R, D + φD − K − R) = 0, so nothing is pulled from E.
The flash loan is repaid with 1,950.975 USDC, Avana's fee of 19.305 USDC goes to the fee recipient, and E receives 70.02 USDC. LiquidationSettled is emitted with permissionless set to true.
Variant: a 1.774998 USDC top-up

Had the USDT leg returned 994 USDC instead, the recovery would be 2,024.25 USDC, below the floor of 2,026.024998 USDC. The gap of 1.774998 USDC is within maxShortfall, so LPVaultSwap pulls it from E and continues with a recovery of 2,026.024998 USDC. Avana's fee stays 19.305 USDC, because it is measured on oracle value. The borrower surplus is 0, as it always is when a shortfall is paid.
Caller payout: 75.049998 − 19.305 = 55.744998 USDC, of which 1.774998 USDC is E's own top-up.
With minPayout at 69 USDC this call reverts with PayoutTooLow. A caller willing to settle at this recovery sets minPayout at or below 55.744998 USDC.
With maxShortfall set to 5 USDC, each leg runs at 124 bps instead of 100 bps (100 + ⌊5 × 10,000 / 2,047.5⌋). A leg below its own minimum reverts with MinOutNotMet and the backup route is tried.
A gap above maxShortfall reverts with RecoveryBelowFloor. A rounding gap at final settlement is paid the same way, or the call reverts with InsufficientProceeds.
Every failure reverts the whole transaction: flash loan, seizure, burn, record debits, deficit report, top-up and payouts. None depends on the pause state, a breaker or a drift reason.

meta.description: When an Avana account can be liquidated, how Aave V4 sizes a partial seizure, and how LPVaultSwap settles it in the repaid debt asset.

strings: Liquidation Design
When an Avana account can be liquidated, how Aave V4 sizes a partial seizure, and how LPVaultSwap settles it in the repaid debt asset.
Overview
Accounts Are Per Market
When an Account Is Liquidatable
Partial Seizure Sized by Aave
LPVaultSwap as the Only Receiver
Exclusivity on a Standard Spoke
Three Entry Points
What Never Blocks Liquidation
What Can Stop Liquidation
Keepers
Fees and Payouts
Deficits and Multi-Debt Accounts
Lens Preview
Not in the Design
One liquidation route on every chain: a partial seizure sized by Aave V4, settled by LPVaultSwap in the debt asset that was repaid.

Avana has one liquidation route on every chain: a partial seizure through LPVaultSwap, settled in the debt asset that was repaid. There is one LPVaultSwap per chain, at a fixed address, serving every Hub, CDP Spoke and market of that chain. In a single transaction it:
flash-borrows the debt asset itself through the chain's flash source, which calls the Aave V3 Pool, or uses the caller's own debt asset when flash liquidity is short;
calls Aave's standard liquidation on the CDP Spoke, which sizes the repayment and the seizure and sends the seized vault tokens to LPVaultSwap;
has the AaveAdapter burn the seized vault tokens, and Collateralization have the market's LP Vault unwind exactly the seized units into the market's tokens;
swaps each token that is not the debt asset into the debt asset over the market's fixed swap routes, each leg with a minimum output derived from oracle prices;
repays the flash loan and its premium, then pays Avana's fee, the caller's reward and any borrower surplus, all in the debt asset.
The borrower keeps the rest of the position and all of its fees. GHO appears only when the debt being repaid is GHO. If any step fails, the whole transaction reverts and the account is unchanged.
The keeper-facing requirements are on the Liquidators page:
Liquidators
Every step of a settlement, with its checks and formulas, is on the flow page:
Liquidation Flow

Each wallet has one PositionProxy per CDP Spoke and market. Each proxy is a separate Aave account that holds exactly one collateral reserve, the market's vault token, and may hold several debt reserves. A wallet using two markets has two accounts, so a falling price in one market never liquidates an account in another market.
The PositionProxy is a logic-free, immutable account. It holds no settlement authority, and its binding to the wallet, the Spoke and the market never changes.
An account can be liquidated when its health factor on the CDP Spoke is below 1 and the prices used for the call are fresh. LPVaultSwap checks each condition below before it moves any funds.
Condition
Rule
Error if not met
Health factor
Below 1, read from the Spoke's account data. Aave applies the same check inside its liquidation call.
NotLiquidatable
Collateral price of the seized market
The market's LP Oracle price is Live or Drifting, not Cached or Expired. Every input is at most its feed's heartbeat plus a 1,800 s margin old, and no feed disagreement pause is active.
StalePrice
Price of the repaid debt reserve
GHO always passes, because Aave prices it at a fixed $1. Any other debt asset needs a Live DebtOracle with every input within its heartbeat plus 1,800 s.
DebtPriceStale
Sequencer gate (Base)
While the sequencer is down, liquidation stops. For 3,600 s after a restart, only accounts with a health factor below 0.95 can be liquidated. Ethereum has no sequencer and is always open.
SequencerDown
SequencerGrace
Recovery grace
For 1,800 s after a market's price recovers from Expired, only accounts with a health factor below 0.95 can be liquidated.
GraceHealthFactor
Hub shares equal assets
The home Hub's added shares equal its added assets for the vault-token asset, so Aave's seized shares equal vault-token units.
SharesNotEqualAssets
Listed market and debt reserve
The market is listed on the account's CDP Spoke (Registered, Active or Offboarding), and the debt reserve is enabled for the Spoke with a funding Hub and an Avana Umbrella recorded.
UnknownMarket
UnknownDebtReserve
Freshness follows each feed's heartbeat

A Chainlink feed publishes on its deviation trigger or after its heartbeat, so an age up to the heartbeat is normal. A USD stablecoin feed with an 86,400 s heartbeat is fresh for 88,200 s: an answer published 23 hours ago passes. A 3,600 s feed is fresh for 5,400 s.
Drifting, disagreement and Expired markets

A market that is Drifting only because of its time-weighted price guard, an observation failure or a price-band breach, with both feed routes of each token fresh and agreeing, can still be liquidated. Aave decides eligibility and sizes the seizure at the served price.

When a token's primary and alternate feeds are both fresh but disagree beyond tolerance, liquidation of that market pauses for up to 3,600 s from the first recorded observation. If they still disagree after that, the market is treated as Expired for liquidation until they agree, a standby price route is switched in, or governance approves a fix.
Once a market is Expired, its collateral counts as almost 0, so the account's health factor falls, but the account cannot be seized until a fresh price returns.
Other debt reserves of the account are not gated. A failing debt price only raises the debt's value, which lowers the health factor, and no debt is ever repaid at a stress price.
How the LP Oracle produces these price states is described on the Price Oracles page:
Price Oracles
Every liquidation goes through Aave's standard
liquidationCall
on the CDP Spoke, called by LPVaultSwap with receiveShares set to false. Aave sizes the repayment and the seizure inside the call. The caller only sets an upper bound on the repayment.
Aave sizes the repayment to bring the account to its target health factor (1.10 is Avana's recommended value; the Aave DAO sets it), with its dynamic liquidation bonus and its dust rule.
The dust rule can require the whole debt in the reserve to be repaid, so callers size their funding for that case.
LPVaultSwap measures the debt repaid and the vault tokens seized as balance changes within the call. It never reads them from Aave's return values or events.
LPVaultSwap does not reimplement Aave's account or liquidation math. Whole-position settlement does not exist, because Aave sizes every seizure itself.
A liquidation that seizes nothing reverts, so debt is never repaid without collateral being taken.

After a liquidation that leaves collateral and is not limited by the dust rule or the collateral cap, the account's health factor is at least Aave's target. The seized value is at most the debt repaid times the bonus, plus one vault-token unit at the served price.

The vault token's transfer rule accepts only three movements: a registered proxy to its home Hub (supply), the home Hub to a registered proxy (withdrawal, burned in the same call), and the home Hub to LPVaultSwap (seizure). Every other recipient is rejected, including zero-amount transfers.
Aave delivers seized collateral with a transfer from the Hub to the liquidator. A liquidation called by any address other than LPVaultSwap therefore reverts on that transfer:
with receiveShares set to true, the Spoke reverts with CannotReceiveShares, because the reserve has share receipt disabled;
with receiveShares set to false and a seizure of at least one unit, the Hub's transfer to the caller reverts with UnauthorizedRecipient and the whole call reverts;
a call sized so that its seizure rounds to 0 units moves no collateral. It only repays debt for the borrower with the caller's own funds.

Every LiquidationCall event on a CDP Spoke that seized vault tokens therefore names LPVaultSwap as the liquidator. No vault token moves, and no deficit is reported, except through LPVaultSwap. An LPVaultSwap upgrade keeps the same proxy address, so it stays the only allowed seizure recipient.

The CDP Spoke is a standard, unmodified Aave V4 Spoke, and its liquidation function has no caller restriction. Exclusivity comes from the vault token's transfer rule together with three Aave settings on every Avana collateral reserve:
Aave setting
Value
What it closes
receiveSharesEnabled
false
A liquidator cannot take the seized collateral as Hub shares instead of vault tokens.
liquidationFee
0, or paid to Avana's fee receiver
