No contract can move the Hub's vault tokens, and Hub shares stay equal to assets.

The listing settings also make the vault-token reserve non-borrowable, list the vault-token asset on no other Spoke (with a draw cap of 0 everywhere), and grant no position-manager approval on any proxy.

The RiskModule checks these settings on every new-account pledge, borrow and withdrawal with debt, and monitoring checks them every block. Drift in any setting trips the market's CONFIG_DRIFT breaker: new pledges, borrows and withdrawals with debt stop, while liquidation, repayment, top-ups, debt-free withdrawal and fee collection continue. The listing payload agreement commits the Aave DAO to keep these settings while Avana debt exists.
Who may call, and with which options, is decided only at LPVaultSwap. Every call liquidates one account, in its one collateral market, against one debt reserve.
Function
Caller
What it does
liquidate
Approved keepers only
The full path, with both route modes (PrimaryThenBackup and BackupOnly). Pays the keeper reward to the caller.
liquidatePermissionless
Any address, with no role, registration or agreement
The same settlement with the PrimaryThenBackup route mode only. Pays the same reward to the caller. It exists so liquidation continues when no approved keeper acts.
settlePending
Any address
Settles vault tokens an earlier, unsettled seizure left at LPVaultSwap. It pays the caller nothing and sends the proceeds to the Avana Umbrella (Coverage Spoke).
A frozen address cannot call either liquidation function. A frozen borrower's own accounts are liquidated like any other.
LPVaultSwap never reads the MarketRegistry's pause state, the pause reason, a circuit breaker or a configuration-drift reason. The three entry points run in every one of these states:
application pause states None, Frozen, Paused(General) and Paused(MintPathSuspect);
any market, debt or POOL_DEPTH breaker tripped;
any Spoke setting drifted (CONFIG_DRIFT);
a market in Offboarding or in its wind-down ramp, and a frozen Aave reserve;
a frozen borrower wallet;
a pool spot price at any distance from the oracle price. There is no pool spot gate, so a moved pool never reverts a liquidation or changes its route mode.

Pause states, breakers and drift stop actions that add risk, such as new pledges and borrowing. They stop no action that reduces risk. A liquidation that cannot run lets an unhealthy account's loss grow toward a deficit, while repayment and debt-free withdrawal stay open anyway.

Example: the Emergency Guardian sets Paused(MintPathSuspect) on the Ethereum Stable LP Hub at 14:00 after an alert on another market. At 14:05 a keeper liquidates an account at a health factor of 0.97 exactly as it would with no pause.
Stale prices of the seized market or the repaid debt reserve, as described above. The account's other debt reserves can still be repaid meanwhile.
The chain's sequencer gate on Base: down, or the grace period after a restart for accounts at or above a health factor of 0.95.

Aave-side halts: a halted or deactivated CDP Spoke on its home or funding Hub, or a paused vault-token or debt reserve. Aave's own errors (SpokeHalted, SpokeNotActive, ReservePaused) pass through unchanged, and Avana cannot override them.
Settlement legs: no usable swap route for a token, or a recovery below the floor that the caller does not top up.

The listing payload agreement commits the Aave DAO to contain a faulty CDP Spoke first with a vault-token reserve freeze and a draw cap of 0, which leave liquidation open. During an Aave halt, keepers keep their liquidations prepared at every block and submit them in ascending health-factor order in the first block after the halt is lifted.

Every approved keeper is Avana's own: its primary keepers and a standby keeper on separate infrastructure. Avana names each address per chain, funds it with that chain's debt assets and pays its gas. Its duty is to liquidate every account below a health factor of 1 on its chains, whatever the account's size, including accounts whose bonus does not cover the gas. Avana has no minimum debt on any chain, and no liquidation depends on a keeper making a profit.
Item
keeperFloor
1 active (approved and unfrozen) keeper per chain, Avana's own
MAX_KEEPERS
addKeeper
Timelock operation at the normal delay (5 days); only the Aave governance executor can cancel it; reverts for a frozen address
removeKeeper
Timelock operation at the short delay (12 hours); reverts if fewer than keeperFloor active keepers would remain

If 0 active keepers ever remain on a chain, the RiskModule halts new borrowing and withdrawals with debt on every CDP Spoke of that chain (LiquidationHalted), while liquidation stays open to anyone through the permissionless path. It halts a debt reserve in the same way when some market token has no usable swap route into its asset (DebtLiquidationHalted). Repayment, fee collection and debt-free withdrawal stay open.

Example: Ethereum has keepers K1 and K2. Removing K2 leaves one active keeper and borrowing continues. A removal of K1 then reverts, because it would leave fewer than keeperFloor. If K1's key were compromised, a replacement keeper is added first and K1 is frozen.

The Aave DAO liquidates Avana accounts through LPVaultSwap like anyone else: through the permissionless path from its executor or any address it controls, at once and with no Avana action, or through the keeper path with a keeper address added by the timelock.
After the flash loan and its premium are repaid, the realized surplus is split in a fixed order, all in the debt asset that was repaid:
Avana's fee: 20% of the oracle-value gain of the seizure, never more than the realized surplus. A caller's routing cannot lower it while the realized gain covers it.
Keeper reward: the rest of the oracle-value gain, capped by what was realized. It goes to the caller of either liquidation function.
Borrower surplus: any recovery above the oracle value of the seized collateral, paid to the borrower's wallet.

This fee is Avana's only on-chain revenue. Avana charges no fee on borrow interest. A payout that its recipient cannot receive goes to the payout escrow (InKindEscrow), credited to that recipient, and never reverts the liquidation.
The formulas and the payout order are on the flow page:

Aave reports a deficit inside its liquidation call only when the call empties the account's collateral and debt remains. It then reports the remaining debt of every borrowed reserve, each on its funding Hub and in that reserve's asset, and zeroes the account's debt. Avana accepts this behaviour unchanged. The Avana Umbrella (Coverage Spoke) of each affected Hub and asset covers its deficit within the coverage window, never with another asset's or another Hub's coverage.
A call that reports a deficit settles like any other. If the recovery floor or the funding check fails, the whole transaction reverts, deficit report included.

After a full seizure, every record of the account stays open with 0 credited units. The depositor can collect fees and take the position back with the AaveAdapter's releaseZeroCredit, which needs no debt check. Keepers skip accounts with no collateral left, because Aave has already reported their deficit.

An account with several debt reserves is liquidated by successive calls, one debt reserve each, in the order the keeper chooses. Keepers continue until the health factor is at least 1, when Aave rejects further calls, or a deficit has been recorded.
The Lens function
previewLiquidation(proxy, debtReserveId, deadline)
the health factor, the bonus, the Spoke's liquidation configuration and every gate evaluated as LPVaultSwap evaluates it;
the debt Aave would repay, sized with Aave V4's pinned liquidation formulas, including the whole-debt case of the dust rule;
the expected seizure, the flash amount sized to the flash source's idle liquidity, the premium, and caller funds for the rest;
the recovery floor, the expected payout and the rounding gap the caller may have to pay.

For a whole-debt close the Lens adds a 500 bps margin to the repayment bound. The Lens is periphery: no Avana contract calls it, and no result of it is used on-chain. On execution, Aave sizes the seizure and LPVaultSwap measures what was spent and seized.
Earlier versions of these docs described mechanisms that are not part of the protocol. None of the following exist:
full-position settlement, settlement modes per market, and in-kind settlement;
swaps through CoW Swap or any other off-chain or batch-settled path;
flash minting from the GHO FlashMinter, and buying the debt asset with GHO;
a protocol settlement budget or any Avana balance that pays settlement gaps;
a keeper-only liquidation rule: liquidation is open to anyone through the permissionless path;
When an Avana account can be liquidated, how Aave V4 sizes the partial seizure, why LPVaultSwap is the only receiver, and what never blocks liquidation.

strings: Welcome
What is Avana?
How It Works
Why LP Collateral Matters
Architecture
Pledge a supported LP position

A borrower pledges an approved Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position to the LP Vault. A Pledge changes custody but does not remove liquidity from the pool. The position keeps earning fees while it is in range.
Represent and value it

The Collateralization Module mints vault tokens 1:1 with the pledged liquidity. The AaveAdapter supplies them to the market's Avana Borrow Spoke through the borrower's Position Proxy. The LPOracle values each vault token from the pool's liquidity math at Chainlink prices, with no haircut. It then checks the result against the pool's TWAP.
Borrow GHO from the Avana Hub

Borrowing capacity is the position's value multiplied by the reserve's Collateral Factor. If capacity is sufficient, the borrower draws GHO from the Avana Hub. A capped GHO credit line from the Aave DAO funds the Hub.
Liquidity stays in the pool

Pledging an LP position moves custody to the LP Vault but leaves its liquidity in the underlying pool. The borrower can borrow GHO without first withdrawing the position and giving up its fees or range.
Valuation and limits are separate
The LPOracle reports the value of the liquidity with no haircut. Each reserve's Collateral Factor, min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor, sets how much of that value supports debt.
Liquidation has explicit rules

Each market has an approved settlement mode. LPVaultSwap uses a flash loan to repay debt and settle the LP collateral in one transaction. Partial settlement removes only the liquidity needed to restore health. Full-position settlement settles the whole position and returns any surplus to the borrower.
Introduction
Avana lets liquidity providers borrow GHO on Aave V4 against their Uniswap v2 and v3 positions. The positions stay active in their pools and keep earning trading fees.
Start with Key Concepts
Explore Borrow Spoke

Avana brings AMM liquidity positions to Aave V4 as collateral. A depositor pledges a Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position to the LP Vault. The depositor then borrows GHO from the Avana Hub while the position stays in the pool.
To borrow against LP assets elsewhere, a liquidity provider usually has to withdraw from the pool first. Withdrawing gives up trading fees and, for concentrated positions, the chosen range.

Avana keeps the position in its pool. The LP Vault holds the position, and a vault token represents it on an Avana Borrow Spoke. A vault token is a transfer-restricted, collateral-only ERC-20 record that maps 1:1 to the underlying liquidity. Avana runs on Ethereum mainnet with selected Uniswap v2 and v3 markets.

Each stage connects a user action to the protocol's accounting. A Pledge establishes custody. Valuation and the Collateral Factor determine borrowing capacity. A borrow creates GHO debt against that capacity. The following guides explain each step in detail.

LP collateral lets assets already deployed in an AMM support a GHO loan. The benefit is capital flexibility, not guaranteed positive carry. Borrowers still bear impermanent loss, price risk and liquidation risk.

The Avana Hub and Avana Borrow Spokes are standard, unmodified Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO. All Avana-specific logic sits in Avana's own contracts: LP Vault, AaveAdapter, LPOracle, RiskModule, CollateralizationModule, LPVaultSwap, AMMSettlementAdapters and AvanaConfig.

Each market category (Stable LP, Correlated LP and Blue-chip/stable LP) has its own Avana Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps. The Avana Hub holds the GHO credit line, and only approved Borrow Spokes can draw from it. A dedicated Position Proxy holds each borrower's Aave position. Deposits, borrows, repayments and withdrawals therefore pass through Avana's controls. The Avana Lend Spoke lets lenders supply assets directly to the Avana Hub. Aave governance approves it separately.
An overview of Avana: pledging Uniswap LP positions, borrowing GHO from the Avana Hub, and the per-market rules for valuation and liquidation.

Responsible disclosure scope and economic-impact triage guidance for Avana security research.

This page describes the scope for responsible disclosure across Avana's own contracts, deployment operations and supporting services. Program terms, rewards, platform and start date are announced separately.

The scope includes direct contract vulnerabilities and economic failures involving LP collateral. Manipulated prices, insufficient liquidity, or vault tokens that no longer match the liquidity in an LPVault can affect borrowing capacity or prevent liquidation from recovering debt.
Severity is based on economic impact.

The assessment considers exploitability and outcomes such as fund loss, unbacked debt, insolvency or systemic collateral mispricing. The size of the affected code is not a measure of the potential loss.

Every Avana contract written from the specification is in scope, together with the deployment scripts, the timelock operations and the calldata builders. Reports are grouped by the affected subsystem. The grouping identifies the component involved; severity depends on the demonstrated impact.
Highest sensitivity
Includes
Primary risks
Why it matters:

Subsystems are triaged separately, but impact is still scored across solvency, user fund safety, liquidation integrity and related protocol risk. The trust boundaries and the stated blast radius of each upgradeable contract are described on this page:
Contract Security

Unmodified Aave V4 code is out of scope, including every Avana Hub, CDP Spoke, Lend Spoke and Coverage Spoke. Avana's deployment check proves their bytecode equals the audited Aave release named in the deployment manifest. The Aave-side settings Avana depends on, and Avana's handling of them, stay in scope under Program C.
Severity is assessed from a credible exploit path and the economic harm it enables, not only from a generic vulnerability score. The levels are the ones used in Avana's audit findings register:
Severity
Meaning
A finding that enables LP overvaluation or bad debt can be critical even if it affects little code. Findings without a credible path to significant economic harm receive a lower severity assessment.

Which contracts can be upgraded and which cannot, the trust boundaries between them, and how far a hostile upgrade can reach.

Avana does not fork, copy or modify Aave V4 code. Every Avana Hub and CDP Spoke is a standard Aave V4 contract owned by the Aave DAO, and all Avana-specific logic sits in Avana's own contracts. Those contracts are split by what they are trusted for: custody, the backing ledger and the seizure checks are immutable, while policy, pricing and liquidation orchestration are upgradeable behind each chain's AvanaTimelock.

The split bounds what a faulty or hostile upgrade can do. Immutable code trusts upgradeable code only for yes-or-no answers, prices and values within bounds, so a bad upgrade can block new activity or misprice within limits, but cannot send a position to anyone but its depositor, release liquidity it did not burn, or stop a borrower from leaving.
The full contract list with addresses and interfaces is on this page:
Reference: Contracts
Form
Contracts
Upgradeable (UUPS behind the AvanaTimelock)
AaveAdapter (one per chain), RiskModule, MarketRegistry, ParameterStore, each LPOracle, each DebtOracle, LPVaultSwap

Borrower actions, eligibility checks, prices, parameters, the pause and breaker state, and liquidation orchestration may need fixes or new integrations. Each upgrade waits 5 days in public and any canceller can stop it.
Immutable

Each LPVault (one per AMM protocol per chain), Collateralization, vault tokens and the VaultTokenFactory, every PositionProxy and the ProxyManager, the Lock, swap-route versions, the flash source implementations, the payout escrow (InKindEscrow), the AvanaTimelock, the Lens

These hold the rules that bound every upgrade: positions return only to their depositor of record, the backing ledger and exposure counters, the seizure share and supply checks, the rule that seized vault tokens go only to LPVaultSwap, the flash-loan checks, escrowed payouts and the timelock's own delays and roles.
Aave DAO contracts
Every Avana Hub, CDP Spoke, Lend Spoke and Avana Umbrella (Coverage Spoke)
Standard Aave V4 contracts, upgraded and configured only by Aave governance. Avana Umbrella Coverage Spokes are not upgradeable.

An immutable component is replaced by deploying a new version and pointing the upgradeable layer at it through the timelock: a new swap route or flash source at the normal delay, or, for an LPVault or ledger fault, offboarding the affected markets and relisting them on fixed contracts. A PositionProxy has no logic, no implementation pointer and no upgrade path; it executes only the AaveAdapter's calls, so account logic changes only with an AaveAdapter upgrade.
The Lens is a read-only periphery contract with no state and no admin. No core contract calls it or depends on what it returns, so it can be replaced at any time.

Each upgradeable contract is a UUPS implementation behind an ERC-1967 proxy. Its upgrade authorization requires APPLICATION_ADMIN, which only the AvanaTimelock holds; a grant of that role or the default admin role to any other account reverts.
No Avana contract has an Ownable owner, a ProxyAdmin or an AccessManager authority. Immutable contracts accept their few privileged calls only from the timelock address fixed in their bytecode.

An upgrade is a timelock operation at the normal delay of 5 days, never below 4. The governance Safe, the Emergency Guardian, the Aave Protocol Guardian and the Aave governance executor can each cancel it during the delay.
Each upgradeable proxy is initialized in its deployment transaction with roles only for the timelock, and the deployer holds no role once deployment ends.
Before each upgrade proposal the invariant suite reruns on a fork after executing the upgrade, and CI compares the storage layout with the deployed version.
The live-configuration check compares every role holder, proxy slot and timelock setting with the deployment manifest after every governance event.

Every place where data, assets or authority cross from one trust domain into another, and what is checked at the crossing:
Boundary
What crosses
What is checked

When an external dependency fails, Avana stops new activity and keeps exits open: a failing price route is replaced by its reviewed standby, a failing swap route by the market's backup route, a short flash source by caller-funded liquidation, and an outage of Avana's backend or app by calling the contracts directly.
If an upgradeable component's implementation is faulty or hostile, its reach is bounded by the immutable layer and by Aave:
Component
Cannot

Borrow against every proxy of its chain up to each draw cap, withdraw supplied vault tokens, mint within the Hub's add cap, burn vault tokens, register proxies, spend allowances granted to it, pledge positions whose owners approved an LPVault
Send a position to anyone but its depositor of record, receive seized vault tokens, change an existing proxy, raise any Aave cap, spend an Avana Umbrella, act on another chain
RiskModule
Approve borrows it should refuse, or block borrowing and pledges
Borrow past Aave's health factor of 1 or the draw caps; touch exits
LPVaultSwap
Liquidate accounts Aave deems liquidatable, at Aave's sizing
Release liquidity it did not burn, because Collateralization checks the share and supply drop; draw any Avana budget, because none exists
MarketRegistry and ParameterStore
Misprice gates within bounds, list bad routes, pause, freeze addresses, trip breakers or keep them latched
Move funds, or block repayment, debt-free withdrawal or fee collection, which read neither contract
DebtOracle
Overprice debt, making accounts liquidatable early within Aave's sizing and bonus, or underprice it
Let accounts borrow past each draw cap or the RiskModule's own debt-price gates
Hostile-component tests

The required audit tests install a hostile AaveAdapter, LPVaultSwap, RiskModule, MarketRegistry and ParameterStore, or PositionProxy implementation through the real AvanaTimelock path at the 5-day normal delay, and show that each effect stays within that contract's stated blast radius:
The immutable LPVault still returns an NFT only to its depositor of record.
Collateralization still rejects a seizure without the matching drop in the account's supply shares and in the vault-token supply.
Borrowing stays within Aave's health factor and the draw caps.

Each chain has one immutable Lock shared by every Avana contract that moves assets or changes accounting. It has exactly two members, the AaveAdapter and LPVaultSwap. Every outer state-changing entry point of either acquires it first, and any attempt to start a second outer entry point in the same call tree reverts.

Every Collateralization entry point and every value-moving LPVault function is reachable only inside a call tree one of the two members opened, and only from its expected caller. The custody contracts check the holder and never acquire.
Swap-route and flash callbacks are accepted only from the route's fixed pool or the chain's Aave V3 Pool while LPVaultSwap holds the Lock.
Vault tokens have no transfer hooks, and position release uses a transfer with no receiver callback.
A shared lock replaces per-contract guards: a guard per contract cannot stop a call that re-enters through a different Avana contract.
The Lock is not a pause or an access list. It never blocks a protocol action at the start of a transaction, and every contract still follows checks-effects-interactions.

Repayment, fee collection, debt-free withdrawal, zero-credit release, pending settlement and liquidation read no pause state, breaker or address freeze, and no Avana contract has a contract-wide pause. Leaving needs one repay per debt reserve, or one repay-all-and-withdraw, and one withdrawal per remaining position, each a single transaction.

Every change that could harm a borrower, such as an upgrade of the AaveAdapter, RiskModule or LPVaultSwap, a new flash source, a looser parameter, a new swap route or a role change, waits the normal delay. The 4-day minimum covers a 3-day borrower reaction time plus those few transactions; on Base it also covers the 12-hour forced-inclusion delay for a borrower who must send a transaction from L1 while the sequencer is down.

Example: an AaveAdapter upgrade on Ethereum is scheduled at t = 1,800,000,000 and is ready at 1,800,432,000. A borrower with GHO and USDC debt on one market and three positions there sends one repay-all-and-withdraw call and two withdrawals within the first hour, long before the upgrade can execute.

The only exception is on the Aave side: a Hub halt of a CDP Spoke or an Aave pause of a reserve stops repayment and liquidation on it. The deployment AIP asks the Aave DAO to contain a Spoke with a reserve freeze and zero draw caps instead, which leave every exit open.
Upgradeable and immutable Avana contracts, trust boundaries, hostile-upgrade blast radius and exit safety.

Overview
What Always Stays Open
Pause States
Transitions and Unpausing
Address Freeze
Circuit Breakers
Alerts Only
Standby Routes
Playbooks
Example: Circuit Breaker
Example: Guardian Pause
Oracle failure, staleness, disagreement or manipulation
The ORACLE gate stops borrowing, withdrawals with debt and new pledges in the market; a failing debt feed stops borrowing that debt.
A guardian switches the failing slot to its standby route; if the standby also fails, the market breaker is tripped while keepers keep liquidating reserves with fresh prices.
Market crash or stablecoin depeg
The stablecoin band and oracle checks stop new borrowing and withdrawals with debt; price drops and seizure surges only alert.
Pause each affected Hub with reason General if more than one market moves, and ask the Aave guardians to freeze the affected reserves; keepers keep liquidating.
Pool or route liquidity drain
POOL_DEPTH, and POOL_SHARE where a pool cap is set, stop new pledges and borrowing; route failures only alert.
Confirm on a fork whether the approved routes can settle at size; only if they cannot, trip the market breaker. Keepers use the backup route and the dead route is disabled at the short delay.
Exploit in progress
Every condition breaker that holds.

Within minutes, pause with MintPathSuspect if minting, the Adapter or Collateralization is suspect, otherwise General; freeze the attacker's addresses; cancel operations the attacker benefits from. The fix is an upgrade at the normal delay.
Malicious or mistaken governance operation
None; the timelock delay is the protection.
Review the calldata within 1 hour and cancel; pause with General if it touches roles or upgrades.
Compromised signer or key
Owner and threshold changes of the governance Safe wait 48 hours.
Cancel every unexpected operation; the Aave governance executor schedules revocation of the compromised roles; a compromised keeper is frozen at once or removed at the short delay.
Keeper outage or misbehaving keeper
With no active keeper, new borrowing on the chain stops.
The standby keeper takes over and the permissionless path stays open; freeze a misbehaving keeper; trip the market breaker on any market left unliquidated past 3,600 seconds.
Bad debt
The DEFICIT breaker freezes borrowing of the reserve above 10,000 GHO outstanding.
The coverage caller covers the deficit from the asset's Avana Umbrella; if the reserve is short, trip the debt breaker and Avana Labs funds it.
Hub liquidity crunch or withdrawal cascade
None on the Avana side; Aave refuses borrows past available liquidity.
Pause with General if new borrowing must stop; keep liquidations running; unpause once utilization is below 90%.
Token issuer action
The ISSUER breaker on every market holding the token and every debt reserve of the asset.
Pause with General if the token is in many markets; ask the Aave guardians to freeze affected reserves; refused payouts go to the payout escrow.
Aave-side incident
The CONFIG_DRIFT check stops new activity.
Follow Aave's incident process; do not unpause until the Spoke matches the deployment manifest.
Frontend or infrastructure compromise
None; the contracts are unaffected.
Take the app offline, warn users, rotate keys and verify the bundle; users exit through a known-good build or a block explorer.
Spoke-setting drift
The market's CONFIG_DRIFT breaker stops new-account pledges, borrowing and withdrawals with debt; seizure stays exclusive to LPVaultSwap.
Ask the Aave Protocol Guardian to freeze the vault-token reserve and set the Spoke's draw caps to 0; trip the breaker manually if no read has yet; the Aave DAO restores the setting.
Flash source short or paused
None; every liquidation reverts before any state change when the source cannot lend.
Keepers switch to their own funds; a lasting failure is answered by a reviewed replacement flash source at the normal delay.
Aave halt of a CDP Spoke
Every new activity on the Spoke is refused; repayment, withdrawal and liquidation stop on the Aave side.
Ask the Aave guardians to replace the halt with a reserve freeze and zero draw caps; pause the Hub with General; keepers prepare liquidations for the first block after the lift.
Sequencer outage (Base)

While the sequencer is down, borrowing and liquidation stop; repay and debt-free withdrawal run through L1-forced transactions. For 1 hour after restart, only accounts below health factor 0.95 can be liquidated.
None on-chain; keepers poke every oracle in the first block after restart and clear the backlog in health-factor order.
Uncovered deficit
The DEFICIT breaker stops borrowing the asset on the affected Spoke.
Ask the Aave DAO to set every drawing Spoke's draw cap to 0; publish the uncovered amount and the adjusted share price; the DAO realizes the loss against that asset's suppliers.
LPVault or ledger bug and relisting
None beyond P-05.
Pause every Hub of the chain (MintPathSuspect when minting or custody is suspect); the Aave guardians freeze affected reserves; offboard the affected markets and relist on fixed contracts.
Debt-asset transfer fee switched on
The ISSUER breaker on every reserve of that asset and every market holding it; liquidation continues.
Confirm the breakers show ISSUER and trip any reserve whose probe did not report; the transfer fee is borne by the keeper's payout.
Fee recipient blocklisted
No liquidation reverts; Avana's fee goes to the payout escrow.
Schedule a new fee recipient at the normal delay; the treasury claims the escrowed fee to an address it names.
Pause states, address freeze, circuit breakers, alerts, standby routes and the playbooks that use them.

Avana has four stops, all held by each chain's MarketRegistry: a pause state per Hub with a reason, a chain-wide address freeze, circuit breakers per market and per debt reserve, and a market's offboarding status. There is no contract-wide pause, no per-function or per-keeper pause, and no incident clock. Each stop blocks new activity only.

The Emergency Guardian (3-of-5 per chain) and the Aave Protocol Guardian act immediately. The governance Safe reaches the same stops through the AvanaTimelock at the short delay, so new activity can still be stopped within 12 hours if both guardians are unavailable. Lifting a stop through the timelock waits the normal delay.
Roles and delays are described on this page:
Governance and Timelock
No pause, freeze, breaker, configuration drift or offboarding can stop these actions:
Repayment by anyone, for any account, including repaying everything and withdrawing in one call
Debt-free withdrawal and partial liquidity removal, and release of a position with no credit
Liquidation of eligible accounts, through both the keeper and the permissionless entry point
Pending settlement and claims from the payout escrow
Rescue top-ups: an indebted account adding collateral within its restore amount, except under Paused(MintPathSuspect)

Stopping liquidation would let unhealthy accounts lose more value with nobody able to close them, turning a code incident into bad debt. Liquidation still needs a fresh price for the market being seized and the debt being repaid, Aave eligibility and an executable swap route. On Base it also waits for the sequencer check. Only Aave-side actions, a Hub halt of a CDP Spoke or an Aave pause of a reserve, can block repayment or liquidation, and the deployment AIP asks the Aave DAO to use them only for exploits and lift them within 48 hours.

Each Hub has one state: None, Frozen or Paused, and a Paused Hub carries a reason, General or MintPathSuspect. The state applies to every market and CDP Spoke whose home Hub it is and to every debt reserve the Hub funds. A borrow reads both the home Hub and the debt reserve's funding Hub and applies the stricter state.
Action
None
Frozen
Paused (General)
Paused (MintPathSuspect)
New pledge by an account with no debt
Top-up or re-credit of an indebted account
Rescue top-up only
Borrow
Withdraw or remove liquidity with debt; repay with collateral
Yes, with every risk check
Repay, repay all and withdraw
Fee collection
Debt-free withdrawal and removal, zero-credit release
Liquidation (keeper and permissionless)
Pending settlement
Blocked calls revert with
ApplicationFrozen
ApplicationPaused
; under Paused(General) a top-up that is not a rescue reverts with
NotRescueTopUp
Frozen stops new exposure from new accounts and new debt while everything that reduces risk keeps working.

Paused(General) also stops withdrawals with debt and every pledge that grows exposure. A rescue top-up stays open, because adding collateral is the cheapest way out of liquidation. A rescue top-up brings an indebted account below the rescue health factor of 1.10 back toward it, within the market's top-up slice.
Paused(MintPathSuspect) is used when the minting code, the AaveAdapter or Collateralization is suspect. It also refuses every top-up and re-credit, rescue included, so no vault token is minted.
Call
Transition
freeze(hub)
None to Frozen
Freeze guardian at once; timelock at 12 hours
pause(hub, reason)
None or Frozen to Paused(reason), or a change of reason while Paused
Pause guardian at once; timelock at 12 hours
unfreeze(hub)
Frozen to None
Pause guardian at once; timelock at 5 days
unpause(hub)
Paused to None
freezeAll()

pauseAll(reason)
Pauses every Hub of the chain not already Paused with that reason
A call on one Hub never changes another Hub, and nothing on one chain changes the other. Use freezeAll or pauseAll when the cause lies in code every Hub of the chain shares.
Unfreezing while Paused reverts with CannotUnfreezeWhilePaused, so a weaker lift cannot silently skip the stronger state. A chain-wide call that changes no Hub reverts with NothingToChange.
A key holding only the freeze role can never undo a freeze, an address freeze or a breaker trip.

The pause state has no on-chain expiry. A guardian that keeps a Hub paused against governance stops only new activity, and its role can be revoked by a role-change operation that only the Aave governance executor can cancel. The other guardian can unpause at once in the meantime.
Each change emits
, and each new reason emits
PauseReasonChanged
freezeAddress
, so an exploiting address loses new activity within minutes without pausing every user. The timelock can do the same at the short delay.
Pledge or re-credit, except as a rescue top-up
Repayment, by the wallet or by anyone for it
Borrow, or receive a borrow
Debt-free withdrawal and removal, repay all and withdraw
Withdraw or remove liquidity with debt, or repay with collateral
Create a new Position Proxy
Pending settlement and payout-escrow claims
Call either liquidation entry point as the caller
Liquidation of the frozen wallet's own positions
Each caller can freeze at most
MAX_ADDRESS_FREEZES_PER_DAY
= 20 addresses in any rolling 24 hours, counted in one-hour buckets, so a compromised guardian cannot freeze users in bulk and the other guardian keeps its full allowance.

Protected addresses cannot be frozen: the timelock, the Aave governance executor, every Avana contract, vault token, LPOracle and DebtOracle, every Hub, approved Spoke and Avana Umbrella, every debt asset, the flash source and the Aave V3 Pool, every recorded swap route and every registered proxy.

A guardian can freeze any keeper, including the last active one. While no active keeper remains, new borrowing stops on every Hub of the chain and liquidation stays open through the permissionless entry point.

Unfreezing an address takes a timelock operation at the normal delay that only the Aave governance executor can cancel, so the guardian that froze it cannot keep it frozen by cancelling every unfreeze. A freeze has no on-chain expiry.

Breakers apply per market and per (CDP Spoke, debt reserve). The RiskModule evaluates them live on new pledges, borrows and withdrawals with debt, so a condition blocks even if nobody recorded it. Avana's keeper calls the permissionless
pokeBreakers
every block to record breaches in the MarketRegistry. LPVaultSwap never reads or writes breaker state, so no breaker can slow or revert a liquidation.
Temporary gates
gateRecoverySeconds
(1,800 seconds, a provisional launch setting within 600 to 7,200) have passed since the last recorded breach.
Gate
Condition
Blocks
ORACLE
The collateral price is not Live, a stablecoin leaves the $0.90–$1.02 band, or a debt price is stale, off source or disagreeing
New borrowing and withdrawals that leave debt
POOL_SHARE
Avana's combined share of a pool, across all borrowers, ranges and Spokes on the chain, is above the pool's cap. Off by default; it applies only where a pool's listing sets a cap
New borrowing and pledges that increase pool exposure
POOL_DEPTH
The pool's in-range liquidity over the TWAP window falls below the listing depth minimum
New pledges and borrowing in the market
Latched security freezes

A security freeze stays tripped until an authorized reset, because a person must confirm recovery. A market breaker blocks new-account pledges, top-ups that are not rescues, borrowing and withdrawals with debt in that market. A debt breaker blocks borrowing that reserve and withdrawals with debt by accounts that owe it.
Reason
Trips when
DEFICIT
The outstanding deficit of a CDP Spoke's debt reserve exceeds breakerDeficitMax: 10,000 GHO for a GHO reserve, a materiality set at listing for other assets
ISSUER
A pool token or debt asset reports itself paused or switches on a transfer fee, read through the issuer probe recorded at listing; a reverting probe counts as tripped
CONFIG_DRIFT
The Aave configuration of the market's CDP Spoke differs from what was listed, including the three required reserve settings
MANUAL
A guardian or the timelock trips the breaker with tripMarketBreaker or tripDebtBreaker
Manual trips: a freeze guardian at once, or the timelock at the short delay.
Resets with
resetMarketBreaker
resetDebtBreaker
: a pause guardian at once, or the timelock at the normal delay.
ConditionStillHolds
Lens shows each breaker's reasons and, for a temporary gate in recovery, when it reopens.

These conditions page on-call but trip nothing on-chain. A reverted liquidation cannot persist a failure count, and an on-chain counter could be fed by a caller to trip it, so monitoring computes them from events and simulations.
Alert
Threshold
Response
Price drop
Guardians decide whether to trip the market breaker
Collateral seized
More than 20% of a market's credited units in 1 hour
Treated as a sign of a price exploit or pool failure
Swap-route failures
Avana's share of a pool
Above 25% across all borrowers and Spokes on the chain
Listing review of the pool's caps
Deficits and Umbrella balance
Every new deficit; an Avana Umbrella below its minimum
Coverage within 72 hours; Avana Labs tops the reserve up
Each listed token records a standby price route beside its primary and alternate Chainlink routes, checked at listing like the slot it can replace. A pause guardian calls
useStandbyRoute(token, slot)
to put it in service at once. The Aave governance executor can undo that switch at once with
cancelStandbySwitch
, and the listed routes come back through a normal-delay operation.

A switch never forces the price Live and never bypasses freshness, validity or the agreement check, so a guardian can only choose among routes the listing reviewed. Each token with a second source also has a standby second source, which a guardian can switch to at once; switching back takes the timelock at the normal delay.

A swap route that fails is disabled at the short delay and restored to its previously approved address at the short delay, an operation only the Aave governance executor can cancel. There is no immediate route block.

Every incident follows the same triage: an alert fires, the on-call engineer confirms it on-chain within 15 minutes, classifies it as one of the playbooks below, pages both Safes and opens an incident log. If it does not yet fit a playbook and new activity is at risk, a guardian first pauses the affected Hub with reason General (P-01), or MintPathSuspect if minting may be involved. A public status note goes out within 1 hour of confirmation and a post-mortem within 7 days.
Each playbook runs on the chain of the incident. On Base, Aave-side steps go through the Base executor and can lag Ethereum, so Base playbooks send the Aave request at detection.
Playbook
Automatic response
Immediate action
Guardian powers are rehearsed on a fork with the real Safes of each chain before launch and every quarter.
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Market 1's pool has an illustrative per-pool cap of 1,000 bps.
Step
What happens

Avana's keeper pokes the breakers every block. At t = 1,000 Avana's share of market 1's pool across all Spokes is 1,040 bps, above the 1,000 bps cap; the MarketRegistry records the breach and emits GateBreached.
A borrow in market 1 reverts with BreakerTripped(1, POOL_SHARE). A pledge that raises pool exposure passes only as a rescue top-up. The borrower can still repay, and LPVaultSwap never reads breakers.
The share falls back below the cap. With gateRecoverySeconds = 1,800 the gate reopens at t = 2,800; the Lens shows it as recovering until then.

Aave records a 10,000 GHO deficit on the CDP Spoke's GHO reserve, equal to breakerDeficitMax. The next poke latches DEFICIT (BreakerLatched) and GHO borrows revert with DebtBreakerTripped. The Lens shows the uncovered amount.
After the deficit is covered, the Emergency Guardian calls resetDebtBreaker for the Spoke's GHO reserve (BreakerReset). While the deficit remained, the same call reverted with ConditionStillHolds.

Alerts only, with no on-chain trip: a 3% price drop in 2 hours, more than 20% of a market seized in 1 hour, 3 swap-route failures in 1 hour. Once routes are confirmed unable to settle at size, the guardian calls tripMarketBreaker.
The app reads the application state and pause reason from the Lens: Paused, MintPathSuspect.
Pledge, re-credit, borrow and repay with collateral on the AaveAdapter revert with ApplicationPaused.
Still open: repay by anyone, fee collection, repay all and withdraw, and liquidation through LPVaultSwap.
Once the mint path is cleared, the guardian changes the reason to General: rescue top-ups reopen, while borrowing and repay with collateral stay blocked until the Hub is unpaused.

Recovery: the pause guardian unpauses the Hub, or the AvanaTimelock does at the normal delay. A milder incident uses a Hub freeze, which stops new-account pledges and borrowing, and an address freeze for a single wallet.

Who can change Avana on each chain, how long each change waits in the AvanaTimelock, who can cancel it, and how the Aave DAO approves markets and credit lines.

Who can change Avana on each chain, how long each change waits, who can cancel it, and how the Aave DAO approves markets and credit lines.

Governance is per chain. Ethereum and Base each have their own AvanaTimelock, a 4-of-7 governance Safe and a 3-of-5 Emergency Guardian Safe, beside the Aave Protocol Guardian and the Aave DAO's executor on that chain. No Avana role, Safe or operation on one chain can act on the other, and no Avana contract accepts a cross-chain message. A change that must apply on both chains is scheduled separately on each, with its own delay and cancellers.

The Aave DAO owns and configures every Avana Hub and Spoke: caps, credit lines, collateral factors, the liquidation settings, reserve freeze and pause, and Hub halts. Every change to Avana's own contracts is an operation on the chain's AvanaTimelock, which Avana Labs cannot bypass. On Base the Aave DAO acts through its Base executor over Aave's cross-chain governance, so Aave-side steps on Base can take longer than on Ethereum.

Every change waits in public before it executes: 5 days for anything that adds risk or new configuration, 12 hours for calls that only reduce risk or stop new activity. Pauses, freezes and breakers stop new activity only. Repayment, fee collection, debt-free withdrawal and liquidation stay open in every governance state.
Authority
Controls
Delay
Aave DAO (governance executor)

Each chain's Avana Stable LP Hub and its CDP, Lend and Coverage Spokes: Spoke deployment and upgrades, the three required reserve settings, collateral factors, caps, reserve flags, bonus curve, target health factor, collateral risk, debt-asset rates, credit lines and draw caps, each Avana Umbrella's coverage ratio and minimum, and the flash-borrower role. On the AvanaTimelock it is the second proposer, a canceller, and the only account that can cancel a role change or a restoring operation. It can undo a guardian's standby price-route switch at once.
Aave governance
Governance Safe (4-of-7 per chain)

Proposes, cancels and executes on its chain's AvanaTimelock: upgrades, the deployment operations and market activation, price sources, routes, parameters, keepers and role changes. It holds no role on any other Avana contract and has no immediate power. A Safe guard limits it to calls to the AvanaTimelock and to itself.
AvanaTimelock (one per chain)
Holds the admin roles on every upgradeable Avana contract and is the fixed timelock address of every immutable one. Runs each ready operation for 14 days after it becomes ready.
As scheduled
Emergency Guardian (3-of-5 per chain)
Freezes and pauses Hubs, freezes addresses, trips and resets circuit breakers, switches a token to its reviewed standby price route or standby second source, and cancels queued operations.
Immediate
Aave Protocol Guardian
The same Avana guardian roles as the Emergency Guardian. On the Aave side, one-way freeze and pause of reserves, so Avana's markets can be stopped without Avana Labs.
Risk service providers (Aave V4)

Set pool risk factors, USD caps, the minimum pledge and any per-pool share cap in each listing package, each with its cap-sizing calculation, and with the Aave DAO the credit lines, draw caps and each Umbrella's coverage ratio and minimum. They hold no on-chain Avana role and propose changes through the governance Safe.
Through the governance Safe

Avana Labs proposes markets and parameter changes for assessment by a designated risk reviewer. The signer sets of the governance Safe, the Emergency Guardian and the Aave Protocol Guardian are pairwise disjoint, so no single group of signers both proposes a change and controls the guardian response to it.

The AvanaTimelock is a non-upgradeable extension of OpenZeppelin's TimelockController. It holds its own admin role and has no other admin, so its proposers, cancellers, delays and settings change only through operations that wait its own delays. On every upgradeable Avana contract it holds both admin roles, and a grant of either role to any other account reverts. Immutable contracts with a privileged function accept that call only from the timelock address fixed in their bytecode. The deployer holds no role once deployment ends.
Setting
Value
Rule
normalDelay
Always between 4 and 5 days. Changed only by a normal-delay operation on the timelock itself.
MIN_NORMAL_DELAY
Immutable floor of the normal delay.
MAX_DELAY
Immutable ceiling of the normal delay.
SHORT_DELAY
Applies only when every call in the operation is on the short-delay list.
SHORT_ELIGIBLE
Fixed set
The only calls the short-delay list may ever hold, fixed at construction. Each one reduces risk, stops new activity or restores configuration already reviewed at the normal delay.
GRACE_PERIOD
A ready operation can be executed for 14 days, then it expires and can only be cleaned up.
publicExecution
true
Anyone can execute a ready operation, so a proposer cannot hold an approved change back to time it.
Required delay

The delay of an operation is read from its calldata, not chosen by the proposer. If every call is on the short-delay list the operation needs 12 hours; one call outside it makes the whole batch wait the normal delay. Scheduling with a shorter delay reverts with this error:
DelayBelowRequired(delay, required)
For example, a batch that only tightens a market cap and disables a swap route needs 43,200 s. Adding one loosening call to the same batch raises the required delay to 432,000 s.
Example timeline

An upgrade scheduled at t = 1,780,000,000 with the normal delay is ready at 1,780,432,000. Anyone can execute it from then until 1,781,641,599. From 1,781,641,600 it is expired and execution reverts. During those 5 days monitoring alerts on the scheduled call, every canceller can cancel it, and a borrower can leave with one repay and one withdrawal per position.

Shortening the normal delay is itself a normal-delay operation, and the new value applies only to operations scheduled after it executes. A cut from 5 to 4 days therefore helps no operation until 9 days after the cut was published.

Four accounts hold the canceller role on each chain: the governance Safe, the Emergency Guardian, the Aave Protocol Guardian and the Aave governance executor. Any of them can cancel a queued operation during its delay, with two exceptions that only the Aave governance executor can cancel:
A role-change operation: every call is a role grant, revoke or renounce on an Avana contract or the timelock.

A restoring operation: every call puts back configuration that was already reviewed, namely restoring a previously approved swap route, switching to a listed standby price route, adding a keeper or unfreezing an address.

This stops a guardian or the governance Safe from blocking its own removal, a replacement's appointment, or a repair that brings back liquidation or an address. The mark needs every call in the batch to qualify: a batch that mixes an upgrade with a role call stays cancellable by every canceller, so a proposer cannot shield a harmful call by adding a role call to it.

Example: a batch that revokes the Emergency Guardian's pause role and also unpauses a Hub is not a role change, so the Emergency Guardian may cancel it. Governance then schedules the revocation on its own. The Emergency Guardian's cancel of that operation reverts, and only the Aave governance executor can stop it. Removing a guardian therefore takes at most one normal delay.

Both guardians, the Emergency Guardian (3-of-5 per chain) and the Aave Protocol Guardian, hold the same two Avana roles on the chain's MarketRegistry and the canceller role on the timelock. Their powers are immediate and either stop new activity or put a route reviewed at listing in service.
Guardians can
Guardians cannot
Freeze or pause one Hub or every Hub of the chain, with a pause reason
Upgrade a contract or change a parameter
Unfreeze and unpause (pause role only)
Choose a price source or route not reviewed at listing
Freeze up to 20 addresses per rolling 24 hours
Unfreeze an address, add or remove a keeper or route
Trip and reset market and debt circuit breakers

Switch a token to its standby price route or standby second source

A new market is listed with one normal-delay batch, so the 5-day delay is its public review, enforced on-chain. The batch deploys the vault token, registers the market with its exact pool and range, sets its initial parameters and caps, and records its price and swap routes. Activation follows at the short delay and reverts unless the Aave-side listing matches.
Every Avana-side risk parameter changes through one process:
Publish: the risk service providers publish the change with its cap-sizing calculation, covering the 48-hour incident term and the tail term for one pool token going to zero.
Build: the governance Safe builds the operation and every signer follows the signing procedure below.
Schedule: the short delay applies only when every call is a tightening; one loosening call makes the whole batch wait 5 days.
Review: monitoring alerts on the scheduled call, and any canceller can cancel during the delay.
Execute: anyone executes it within 14 days of its ready time. Each setter re-checks its bounds at execution, so a value that became unsafe while queued reverts.
Confirm: the live-configuration check and the Lens cap headroom confirm the result.
Loosening limits

Each parameter has separate tighten and loosen setters. A tightening must be strictly safer and stays within the hard and liveness bounds, with no step limit. A loosening is limited in size and frequency:
Parameter
Largest loosening step
Any USD cap (market, token, depositor, top-up slice)
slippageAllowanceBps
+25 bps

Every step-limited parameter

For example, from a market cap of $2,000,000 one loosening reaches at most $3,000,000, and the next loosening of that cap executes no earlier than 5 days later, each with its own public review. A larger step reverts with
LoosenStepTooLarge
, and an early one with
LoosenTooSoon
. The stablecoin band limits, the grace duration and the grace health factor change only at the normal delay in both directions.
Collateral-factor changes

The collateral factor itself is an Aave value changed by AIP. For a cut, Avana first tightens the pool risk factor at the short delay, so the drift check stops new borrowing while Aave's factor is above the new expected one, and the Aave payload then lowers it. For a raise, the Avana change at the normal delay executes first. Aave-side values such as the bonus curve, target health factor, caps, credit lines and Umbrella settings change only through Aave governance.
Keepers hold no role: LPVaultSwap keeps a list of approved addresses. Avana runs its own keeper on each chain and pays its gas. The list changes only through the timelock:
Adding a keeper waits 5 days and only the Aave governance executor can cancel it, so no guardian can block a replacement.
Removing a keeper waits 12 hours and reverts if it would leave fewer active keepers than the keeper floor of 1.

A guardian can freeze a misbehaving keeper's address at once, even the last active one. While no active keeper remains, new borrowing on the chain stops, and anyone can still liquidate through the permissionless entry point.
Keeper keys are rotated by adding the new key first (5 days) and removing the old one after (12 hours).

Step
What it decides

Confirms support for the assessment
Deployment ARFC and Snapshot

Lists each CDP Spoke as a standard Aave V4 Spoke with the three required reserve settings, grants the flash-borrower role on each chain's Aave V3 Pool, sets each Spoke's liquidation settings, registers an Avana Umbrella for GHO on each Stable LP Hub, and adds the Aave executor and Aave Protocol Guardian to each AvanaTimelock
Funding ARFC and Snapshot
Sets the GHO credit line and draw caps per chain, the coverage ratio and minimum of each Avana Umbrella, and a flat GHO rate at or above the Core Hub GHO base rate
AIPs
Put both approved proposals on-chain; on Base through the DAO's Base executor
Neither follow-up ARFC activates borrowing on its own: launch needs both, plus every security and risk prerequisite. Each chain beyond Ethereum and Base comes through its own ARFC.
Credit line request

The request is an initial credit line of 2,000,000 GHO on the Ethereum Stable LP Hub. The Base line is set in the funding ARFC, within the GHO flash liquidity of the Aave V3 Base Pool and the depth of the Base swap routes. Capacity scales toward 10,000,000 GHO only as live performance criteria are met, and each increase needs governance approval. Each CDP Spoke's draw cap stays within its chain's flash liquidity, swap-route depth and the Umbrella coverage bound.
Avana recommends a target health factor of 1.10 and a minimum liquidation bonus of at least 2% for each CDP Spoke. The Aave DAO decides both in the listing AIP.
This standard applies on each chain to the governance Safe, the Emergency Guardian, the Avana treasury Safe and the keeper operators.

Every Safe signer key is on a dedicated hardware wallet that shows EIP-712 typed data on the device. No hot keys, browser-extension keys or shared devices. Keeper operators keep keys in their own HSM or KMS.
At most 3 of the 7 governance Safe signers belong to Avana Labs, and the signers span at least 3 independent organisations and 3 jurisdictions.
The Emergency Guardian has 5 different people across at least 3 time zones.
No person signs on two Safes of the same chain, and the Aave Protocol Guardian's signers are disjoint from both.

For every transaction each signer decodes the calldata from the raw transaction, recomputes the Safe transaction hash against the device, simulates it on a fork and checks that its required delay matches the intended class. Two signers also check every target against the deployment manifest.
Every signer sends a signed liveness message each month, and monitoring alerts when fewer than threshold + 1 signers answer within 72 hours.
A departing or suspect signer is replaced within 72 hours, and every key is rotated at least every 24 months.
A delay module makes every owner and threshold change of a governance Safe wait 48 hours.
Each quarter both chains' Safes rehearse on a fork: pause and unpause, address freeze, standby switch, breaker trip and reset, and a schedule-and-cancel drill.

The Aave governance executor is a second proposer beside the governance Safe on each chain. If a Safe loses its quorum or renounces its role by mistake, repairs still reach the timelock through Aave governance, which every canceller watches. If the governance Safe stops acting, every contract keeps running on its current configuration, queued operations stay executable within their grace window, the guardians keep their immediate powers and the Aave DAO keeps every Aave-side control.

Handover to the Aave DAO is one role-change operation per chain: it grants the executor role to the Aave governance executor, grants the proposer and executor roles to a second DAO-named holder, and revokes the governance Safe's roles last, so the proposer set never falls below two. The guardian and canceller roles are unchanged, and the admin roles stay with the timelock.

strings: Avana Umbrella
Avana Umbrella, the First-Loss Reserve: one Coverage Spoke per Hub and debt asset, funded by Avana Labs and controlled by the Aave DAO, that eliminates recorded deficits within 72 hours.
Overview
Form and Control
How a Deficit Arises
Covering a Deficit
Sizing and the Coverage Rule
Deficit Breaker
Funding and Withdrawals
Losses Beyond the Reserve
Walkthrough
What It Does Not Cover
The First-Loss Reserve: one Coverage Spoke per Hub and debt asset, funded by Avana Labs and controlled by the Aave DAO.

Avana Umbrella is Avana's protocol safety module, named after Aave's Umbrella, whose design inspired it. It is the First-Loss Reserve: one Coverage Spoke per (Hub, debt asset), funded by Avana Labs in that asset and controlled by the Aave DAO. Each one covers the deficits Aave records for approved Avana CDP Spokes in its own asset, on its own Hub, and nothing else.

At launch there are two: GHO on the Ethereum Stable LP Hub and GHO on the Base Stable LP Hub. Every further debt asset enabled on a CDP Spoke, such as USDC, USDT or WETH, gets its own Coverage Spoke, funded to its minimum before any draw cap on that asset rises above 0.

The Coverage Spokes are Avana's only on-chain loss layer. Avana counts no coverage from committed fee income, from Aave's own Umbrella or from DAO layers. Collateral limits and liquidation remain the first controls against loss.

A Coverage Spoke is a supply-only Spoke registered on its asset of its Hub with a draw cap of 0. Its funds are Hub liquidity of that asset like any other supply, held as shares, and accrue the asset's supply yield.

It is not upgradeable and has no owner other than the Aave DAO's access manager. Avana Labs and Avana contracts hold no role on it. A replacement is a new deployment, funded through the old one's withdrawal path.
The Coverage Spokes are the only holders of the Hub's deficit-eliminator role, and each spends its shares only through the Hub's deficit elimination on its own asset.
The Aave DAO sets each one's allowlist of CDP Spokes, its minimum balance and its withdrawals. A DAO-delegated caller holding the coverage role triggers coverage.

Each account is one Position Proxy per (wallet, CDP Spoke, market), so it holds exactly one collateral reserve. A deficit arises only when a liquidation through LPVaultSwap empties that reserve while debt remains. Inside the liquidation, the CDP Spoke reports the remaining debt of each debt reserve to that reserve's funding Hub, in that reserve's own asset, and the account's debt in it becomes 0.

A liquidation that reverts records nothing. The deficit stays counted against the CDP Spoke's draw cap on that asset until it is eliminated, so it uses draw-cap headroom. Monitoring warns on any non-zero deficit at once and pages if one is still uncovered after 24 hours.
The coverage caller covers every recorded deficit within
deficitCoverageWindow
, 72 hours from the deficit being recorded. On Base the window includes the delivery time of Aave's cross-chain governance to the Base executor, so the Base runbook starts the call at the first page.
The caller calls
coverDeficit(borrowSpoke, maxAmount)
on the Coverage Spoke of the deficit's Hub and asset.
The call reverts unless the caller holds the coverage role, the CDP Spoke is on the allowlist and a deficit is recorded.
The Coverage Spoke calls
eliminateDeficit
on its Hub for its own asset. The Hub burns the matching shares, rounded up so other suppliers' share price does not fall, and reduces the recorded deficit.
A deficit in two assets takes two calls, one on each asset's Coverage Spoke. A shortfall in one asset's reserve is never made up from another asset, Hub or chain.
The amount covered in one call:
amount = min(maxAmount, recorded deficit rounded up, fundedBalance())
Coverage never exceeds what the caller asked for, what Aave recorded as lost, or what the reserve holds. It keeps working while the Coverage Spoke or the covered CDP Spoke is halted on the Hub.

The funding ARFC sets each reserve's coverage ratio and minimum balance with Aave's risk service providers. The funded balance must cover a fixed share of every draw cap on its (Hub, asset), summed over every CDP Spoke that draws that asset from that Hub:
fundedBalance × 10⁴ ≥ coverageRatioBps × Σ drawCap
The rule is checked when a debt reserve is enabled and on every draw-cap raise Avana records. A raise that would break it reverts with
CoverageBelowRatio

Example values; the funding ARFC sets the real ones. At an illustrative ratio of 20% (2,000 bps), a 2,000,000 GHO credit line on the Ethereum Stable LP Hub needs at least 400,000 GHO in its Umbrella. Raising one Spoke's draw cap from 1,200,000 to 1,250,000 GHO, so that the summed caps reach 2,050,000 GHO, needs at least 410,000 GHO; until Avana Labs funds 10,000 GHO more, the raise reverts.

Beyond the ratio, caps are sized so that each reserve covers two modelled losses per (Hub, debt asset): an incident term over a 48-hour window, which includes a debt-asset price rise, and a tail term for one pool token going to zero. The Lens reports the cap-based tail coverage, and monitoring warns below 150% of the minimum and pages below 100%.
When the outstanding deficit of a CDP Spoke's GHO reserve exceeds
breakerDeficitMax

, 10,000 GHO, the DEFICIT breaker freezes new borrowing on that debt reserve automatically. Other debt assets set their own materiality level at listing. Smaller deficits trip nothing on-chain; every new deficit raises an alert and is covered within 72 hours.
The breaker latches. It stays tripped after coverage until a pause guardian calls
resetDebtBreaker
, or the timelock does at the normal delay, so the root cause is reviewed before borrowing resumes. The reset reverts with
ConditionStillHolds

A reserve below its minimum raises a monitoring alert and trips no breaker. The Emergency Guardian or the Aave Protocol Guardian decides whether to trip a manual debt breaker or freeze the Hub, and Avana Labs tops the reserve up. Repayment, debt-free withdrawal, liquidation and borrowing of other assets continue throughout.

Avana Labs funds each reserve to at least its minimum before any draw cap on its (Hub, asset) rises above 0, and tops it back up after any coverage. The funding call moves the asset straight to the Hub and credits it as the Coverage Spoke's shares; funds added give the funder no claim.
Avana's committed fee share counts toward the minimum only once received in that asset through the funding call.
Pending-settlement proceeds go to the Umbrella. When anyone calls
settlePending

to clear vault tokens left by a seizure that never settled, LPVaultSwap converts the released tokens into the market's settlement debt asset (GHO at launch) and funds the matching Umbrella with the amount recovered.
Funds leave only through deficit elimination or a DAO withdrawal: the Aave DAO requests it, and it executes after
reserveWithdrawalDelay
, 14 days, fixed in the contract.

Before the credit line closes, the DAO approves a withdrawal only if the balance left still meets the minimum. Unused capital returns to Avana Labs only after that (Hub, asset) credit line closes and every allowlisted CDP Spoke has zero debt and zero deficit in that asset.

A deficit larger than the reserve's funded balance stays recorded on the funding Hub. The uncovered part is a loss of that Hub asset's suppliers, pro rata to their shares, including suppliers through the chain's Lend Spoke.

Aave's share accounting counts the deficit inside the asset until the loss is realized, so a supplier who withdrew before realization would leave at full value. Avana removes that information advantage. As soon as an uncovered deficit appears, the Emergency Guardian runs playbook P-18:
Every drawing Spoke's draw cap on that (Hub, asset) is set to 0 through the Aave Guardian.
Monitoring raises the
UncoveredDeficit(hub, asset, amount)
alarm, which goes to lenders through the app.
The Lens publishes the uncovered amount and the deficit-adjusted share price, so every lender sees the loss before withdrawing.
The Aave DAO realizes the uncovered amount against supplier shares. A top-up by Avana Labs or the DAO before realization lets the coverage caller eliminate the remainder instead.
priceAdj = (A − uncovered) / Sh

Example values (Ethereum, GHO): the Hub's GHO has A = 2,000,000 GHO and Sh = 1,950,000 shares. A deficit of 130,000 GHO meets a reserve holding 100,000 GHO, because earlier coverage drew it below its 400,000 GHO minimum. After coverage 30,000 GHO stays uncovered. The Lens shows an adjusted price of (2,000,000 − 100,000 − 30,000) / (1,950,000 − 97,500) ≈ 1.00944 GHO per share, against an unadjusted 1.02564. A lender holding 18,525 shares, 1% of the remaining shares, bears 300 GHO of the loss once it is realized.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Market 1 is the USDC/USDT 0.01% Uniswap v3 market on the Uniswap v3 Stable CDP Spoke of the Ethereum Stable LP Hub, with a collateral factor of 28.12% and a maximum liquidation bonus of 5%. Dan's proxy holds 20,000 vault tokens at $2.00 ($40,000) and owes 10,000 GHO, a health factor of 1.1248. The GHO Umbrella holds an illustrative 400,000 GHO, its minimum. The Hub's GHO has A = 2,050,000 GHO and Sh = 2,000,000 shares, and GHO draw caps sum to 2,000,000 GHO.
Step
What happens
1. Collapse

USDT collapses within minutes and the LPOracle serves $0.50 per vault token. Dan's collateral is worth $10,000 and his health factor is 0.2812. USDT leaves the $0.90–$1.02 stablecoin band, so new borrowing and withdrawals that leave debt stop in market 1; the price-drop alert fires. Liquidation continues.
2. Preview
Avana's keeper previews the liquidation through the Lens: the bonus is the maximum 5%, and the collateral covers only 10,000 / 1.05 = 9,523.81 GHO of debt, so the preview flags a deficit.
3. Liquidation
Through LPVaultSwap, Aave seizes all 20,000 vault tokens and restores 9,523.81 GHO. Dan's only collateral reserve is now empty, so the Spoke reports a deficit of 476.19 GHO. Dan's debt is 0.
4. Settlement
The unwind and swaps return 9,950 GHO, above the 9,899 GHO minimum. Of the 426.19 GHO gain, Avana's fee is 95.24 GHO (20% of the 476.19 GHO oracle gain) and the keeper receives 330.95 GHO.
5. Alert
Monitoring sees the deficit and warns at once. It is below 10,000 GHO, so the DEFICIT breaker does not trip and GHO borrowing on other markets continues.
6. Coverage
Within 72 hours the coverage caller calls coverDeficit with a limit of 1,000 GHO. The amount is min(1,000, 476.19, 400,000) = 476.19 GHO.
7. Elimination
The Hub burns 464.576 shares from the Coverage Spoke, rounded up, and the Spoke's deficit is 0.
8. Below minimum
The reserve now holds about 399,523.81 GHO, below its 400,000 GHO minimum. The contract emits ReserveBelowMinimum and monitoring alerts. Repayment, liquidation and debt-free withdrawal run as normal.
9. Top-up
Avana Labs funds 477 GHO and the reserve is back above its minimum.

Shortfalls inside a liquidation. A liquidation that cannot reach its recovery floor reverts with nothing changed, or its caller pays the gap through the shortfall top-up. Rounding gaps from Aave's dust rule are paid by the liquidating keeper.
Keeper gas and keeper losses, which Avana pays from its own keeper budget.
Borrowers' own losses. Borrowers still bear impermanent loss, price risk and liquidation risk; the reserve does not raise borrowing capacity.
Another asset, Hub or chain. Each chain's instances are sized against that chain's caps only.

Risk Framework
The layers that limit loss in Avana's Aave V4 markets, from account isolation and caps to liquidation, Avana Umbrella and governance limits.

Avana lists AMM liquidity positions as collateral on standard, unmodified Aave V4 Spokes owned by the Aave DAO. Every Aave contract stays unmodified; custody, valuation and liquidation sit in Avana's own contracts. Risk is limited in layers, each with its own owner and parameters, and every market sets its own values at listing.

The Aave DAO owns and configures every Avana Hub and Spoke and can stop Avana's markets without Avana Labs. Every change to Avana's own contracts waits in the AvanaTimelock, which Avana Labs cannot bypass. No pause, freeze or breaker stops repayment, debt-free withdrawal, fee collection or eligible liquidation.

AvanaTimelock and fixed bounds

A market is one pool with one exact tick range, listed as one collateral reserve on one CDP Spoke. Each wallet gets one Position Proxy per (CDP Spoke, market): a logic-free, immutable Aave account bound to that wallet, Spoke and market. Each market therefore has its own health factor, and nothing is cross-collateralized across markets.
An account holds at most 16 positions in one market, so the liquidation of its last part always fits in one transaction.
Each pledged position must match a listed market's exact pool and range, with a minimum value of $10. Aerodrome Slipstream positions must be unstaked.
There is no borrower allowlist and no minimum debt.
Borrowers in the same market still share exposure to its oracle, contracts and pool liquidity.

Valuation and borrowing limits are separate. The LPOracle values the vault token at its fair composition at Chainlink prices, with no haircut. The reserve's collateral factor then sets how much of that value can support debt. It starts from the lowest Aave V4 Core Hub collateral factor among the pool's tokens and applies the pool risk factor once, rounding down:
LP Collateral Factor = min(CF₁, …, CFₙ) × Pool Risk Factor

The pool risk factor is at most 40% and reflects the position's range, price sensitivity, pool depth and expected liquidation costs. A GHO leg uses an explicit factor set at listing. The Aave DAO sets the reserve's factor at or below this value and never at 0 while accounts hold the reserve; Avana's drift check stops new borrowing if Aave's factor is set higher. Gauntlet's analysis of LP collateral recommends conservative starting factors, and final factors are calibrated per market with service providers.

Aave's rule is the only on-chain borrowing limit: an account may borrow up to a health factor of 1.00. The Lens shows a recommended borrow at 1.10 beside that maximum, because a loan opened at full capacity has no buffer. An optional per-market hard health floor exists, off at launch, and is set only if stress tests justify it.

The risk service providers set every cap in each market's listing package, with its cap-sizing calculation. Caps are charged at the USD value at pledge, booked at no less than a stress floor of $1.00 per whole vault token.

Credit line and draw caps

Set by the Aave DAO; each draw cap stays within the chain's flash liquidity, swap-route depth and the Avana Umbrella coverage rule

Concentration is covered by the token and market caps and listing review rather than a default pool-share limit: removing liquidity has no price impact, and liquidation proceeds can be sold through any approved route. Caps are sized so that each Avana Umbrella covers two modelled losses: the 48-hour incident term, which includes each pool's worst historic LP drop and a debt-asset price rise, and the tail term for one pool token going to zero. Tightening a cap takes 12 hours; raising one takes 5 days and at most +50% per step.

Each token has a Chainlink primary route, an alternate route with automatic failover and a standby route approved at listing. A feed counts as fresh for its own heartbeat plus 1,800 seconds, and stablecoins are never valued above $1. A 30-minute pool TWAP is a consistency check, not a price source, and borrowing also needs each token's price to agree with an independent second source.
Condition
Market response
Live, second source agrees
Normal operation
Live, second source disagrees or is unavailable
Borrowing and withdrawals that leave debt are blocked. Pledges, repayment and liquidation continue.
Drifting: TWAP consistency check fails

New pledges, borrowing and withdrawals that leave debt are blocked. Aave values the collateral at the lower of the fresh and last accepted price. Liquidation continues while the Chainlink inputs are fresh.
Drifting: primary and alternate routes disagree

Borrowing is blocked and the collateral is valued at the lower route. Liquidation of the market waits until the routes agree, a guardian switches the faulty route to its standby, or a timelock fix executes.
Cached: both routes of a token stale or invalid, for up to 1 hour
Pledges, top-ups and borrowing are blocked. Aave values the collateral at the last accepted price. Liquidation of the market waits for a fresh price or a standby switch.
Expired: after 1 hour of Cached
The collateral counts as worthless in Aave's health factor. Liquidation of the market waits for a fresh price or a standby switch, so collateral is never seized at a price Avana cannot trust.
First 30 minutes after recovery from Expired
Only accounts below a health factor of 0.95 can be liquidated.
Base sequencer down, or within 1 hour of its restart
Borrowing is blocked. Liquidation pauses while the sequencer is down; for 1 hour after restart only accounts below 0.95 can be liquidated.

In every row, repayment, fee collection and debt-free withdrawal stay open. A stablecoin outside the $0.90–$1.02 band also blocks new borrowing and withdrawals that leave debt. A non-GHO debt asset follows the same states through its DebtOracle, except that once Expired it serves a raised stress price, so debt is never undervalued.
Temporary gates (ORACLE, POOL_SHARE, POOL_DEPTH) stop new activity in a market while their condition holds and reopen after 30 minutes of healthy observations.

Latched freezes (DEFICIT, ISSUER, CONFIG_DRIFT, MANUAL) stay tripped until a pause guardian or the timelock resets them. The deficit freeze trips when a CDP Spoke's outstanding GHO deficit exceeds 10,000 GHO.
Each Hub has a pause state: None, Frozen, Paused(General) or Paused(MintPathSuspect). Guardians can also freeze or pause every Hub of a chain at once.
A guardian can freeze up to 20 wallets per rolling 24 hours; a frozen wallet loses new activity, never its exits.
Price drops, seizure surges, swap-route failures and pool concentration above 25% are alerts, not on-chain trips.

Emergency Controls
An account becomes liquidatable when its health factor falls below 1. Every liquidation runs through LPVaultSwap in one atomic transaction and is always partial:
LPVaultSwap flash-borrows the debt asset from the Aave V3 Pool, or the caller funds it.

It calls the CDP Spoke's standard liquidation, which sizes the repayment toward the Spoke's target health factor (Avana recommends 1.10) with Aave's dynamic bonus, and receives the seized vault tokens.
The seized tokens are burned and exactly that share of the position is unwound; the borrower keeps the rest of the position and all of its fees.

Each unwound token is swapped into the debt asset over the market's primary or backup route, with oracle-derived minimum outputs, and the proceeds must reach a recovery floor. A keeper may top up a small shortfall from its own funds; otherwise the transaction reverts and nothing changes.
Avana's fee is 20% of the oracle gain; the keeper receives the rest of the realized gain and any further surplus goes to the borrower. A payout a token refuses goes to the payout escrow.

Avana runs its own keeper on each chain and pays its gas, liquidating every account below 1 whatever its size. Any address can also liquidate through the permissionless entry point. A direct liquidation from any other contract fails, because the vault token accepts seized collateral only to LPVaultSwap and every Avana reserve has three required settings: shares not received, no Aave liquidation fee and no reinvestment controller.

No Avana pause, breaker, configuration drift or address freeze stops liquidation. It waits only for a fresh price of the seized market and the repaid debt, the Base sequencer check, and Aave-side halts or reserve pauses. The full flow and examples are on this page:
Liquidation Framework

When a liquidation empties an account's collateral while debt remains, Aave records a deficit on the funding Hub in that debt asset. Each (Hub, debt asset) has its own Avana Umbrella, a Coverage Spoke funded by Avana Labs and controlled by the Aave DAO, which eliminates a recorded deficit within 72 hours. At launch there are two, GHO on each chain's Stable LP Hub. A loss larger than the reserve falls on that Hub asset's suppliers, pro rata, after the Aave DAO realizes it.

Each chain has its own AvanaTimelock, 4-of-7 governance Safe and 3-of-5 Emergency Guardian; nothing on one chain acts on the other.

Every upgrade, parameter change, market listing and role change waits 5 days, never less than 4. Calls that only reduce risk or stop new activity wait 12 hours. Anyone can execute a ready operation within 14 days.

The governance Safe and the Aave governance executor propose. The governance Safe, both guardians and the Aave governance executor can cancel; only the Aave governance executor can cancel a role change or a restoring operation.
Loosening is limited: a USD cap rises at most 50% and the slippage allowance at most 25 bps per step, once per normal delay.
Guardians cannot upgrade, change parameters, choose a new price source, unfreeze an address or move funds.
Avana Labs proposes markets and parameter changes for assessment by a designated risk reviewer, and new markets are listed at the normal delay, a 5-day public review enforced on-chain.
